d16c43d6a583aea6: SIBU, Nov 7 — A 19-year-old youth died after being stabbed in the chest during an incident at a public park along Jalan Gambir here around midnight last night.
The victim was reportedly at the park with a group of young men and women when an argument broke out, allegedly leading to the stabbing.
He sustained a stab wound to the chest and was rushed to hospital for emergency treatment but later succumbed to his injuries.
It is understood that nearby residents heard a woman screaming from the direction of the park, prompting them to alert the police.
Police are believed to have arrested two men in their 20s to assist in investigations.
When contacted today, Sibu District Police Chief ACP Abang Zainal Abidin Abang Ahmad confirmed that the case was still under investigation.
“The case is still under further investigation,” he said. — The Borneo Post
8096a43e8c94cbbb: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — The security presence outside former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s residence was nowhere to be seen today, a day after the Taman Duta property was placed under tight security ahead of his anticipated return under house arrest.

According to Astro Awani, no police officers or Prisons Department vehicles were visible outside the Jalan Langgak Duta residence, while yellow security tape restricting access to the property had also been removed.
The scene contrasted sharply with Friday, when security personnel controlled access to the residence, allowing only authorised individuals and vehicles to enter or leave.

The heightened security came as preparations were made for Najib’s expected return after he paid a RM50 million fine in the SRC International corruption case, fulfilling a key condition of a royal pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028.
However, the move was put on hold after the Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) called for further legal clarification on the implementation of the conditional pardon.
Despite the absence of security personnel today, local and international journalists remained stationed near the residence, awaiting further developments.
Najib’s residence was officially gazetted as a prison on Friday under Section 3 of the Prisons Act 1995, following a declaration by Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
The designation covers the property and its surrounding land, allowing it to be used for the detention of individuals in lawful custody.
In a statement today, the AGC called for an urgent court determination on whether Najib’s SRC International prison sentence remains in force or has legally ended following the payment of the fine.

It said the distinction was crucial because Najib’s separate 15-year prison sentence in the 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) corruption case was ordered to begin after the completion of his SRC International sentence.

The AGC also rejected allegations that it was challenging the authority of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, maintaining that its request for judicial clarification was intended to ensure the royal decree and existing court orders were implemented lawfully.

The clarification came after Istana Negara said the conditional pardon granted to Najib was clear and unambiguous, warning that any attempt to dispute the decree could amount to defying the King’s order.
Najib, 73, has been serving a prison sentence since August 2022 following his conviction for offences involving RM42 million in SRC International funds.
His original 12-year sentence was reduced to six years under a partial royal pardon in 2024, while his RM210 million fine was cut to RM50 million.
A subsequent conditional pardon granted on September 18 this year allowed him to serve the remaining term under house arrest, subject to payment of the fine and compliance with stipulated conditions.
703cbeadeebd6600: MELAKA: The government has not issued any directive for the public to stock up on food supplies for a 72-hour period as recommended by the Federation of Malaysian Consumer Associations (Fomca).
Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu advised consumers not to panic buy, but instead to continue shopping according to their daily needs as usual.

"We do acknowledge that we are concerned about the current situation, including cyber threats, but we have not yet reached the stage of issuing directives for the public to stockpile food supplies," he said at a press conference after launching the 'Himpunan Semarak Tani Jualan Agro Madani' in Bukit Katil.

Yesterday, Fomca advised consumers to stock up on food and basic necessities for a period of at least 72 hours, as a precautionary measure against potential supply disruptions due to global geopolitical uncertainties and natural disasters.
Mohamad assured that the national rice stock is currently sufficient for a period of six months and will continue to be increased.
"The supply of frozen fish is also guaranteed to be sufficient for the next eight months. So, there is no need for excessive purchases.
"Buying goods in excessive quantities will only create problems and make it difficult for other consumers to obtain supplies," he said.

He said that the Agriculture and Food Security Ministry is also constantly assessing the current situation, including through collaboration with universities and researchers such as climate change experts.

As an initial preparatory step, he said the Fisheries Development Authority (LKIM), along with private traders who have freezing facilities, have been asked to stock up especially on the people's choice of fish in high demand in the market.
In another development, he said the government aims to implement 5,000 Agro Madani Sales programmes nationwide, compared to the 3,400 programmes that have been held so far.
Mohamad said this programme that allows consumers to buy goods at 10 to 30 per cent cheaper prices aims to ease the people's cost of living burden, especially in rural and small town areas.

"We cannot hold programmes like these every day because local grocery stores also need to do business. So, we are holding it weekly to give people a chance to save money while also ensuring the sustainability of local traders," he added.

c2337ee578f9d79b: PETALING JAYA: DAP has yet to discuss who will take over the transport minister's position following party secretary-general Loke Siew Fook’s decision to resign from the Cabinet, vice-chairman Syahredzan Johan said.
Syahredzan said that for now, Loke’s resignation has not taken effect as former prime minister Najib Razak has yet to begin serving the balance of his current jail sentence under house arrest.
“Therefore, it would not be appropriate to discuss who his replacement would be.

"When the time comes, the composition of the Cabinet is the prime minister’s prerogative. The prime minister will, of course, make a decision after consulting the DAP secretary-general," Harian Metro quoted him as saying.
Yesterday, Loke said his resignation from the Cabinet post would take effect the moment Najib "enters his home".
Loke, who was appointed transport minister in 2022, tendered his resignation in September, after Najib was granted a conditional pardon.
However, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim urged him to continue his duties until Najib was released.

Umno said yesterday it had settled the RM50 million fine, which is one of the conditions attached to the conditional pardon by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, Sultan Ibrahim, following a crowdfunding initiative.
Najib was jailed in August 2022 after the Federal Court upheld his conviction for abuse of power, criminal breach of trust and money laundering involving RM42 million in SRC International funds.
He was sentenced to 12 years’ jail and fined RM210 million.
In January 2024, then Yang di-Pertuan Agong, Al-Sultan Abdullah Sultan Ahmad Shah halved his prison sentence and reduced his fine to RM50 million as part of a royal pardon.

Two months ago, Sultan Ibrahim granted Najib a further conditional pardon, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, provided he paid the fine and complied with all other stipulated conditions.
6b774cf119bed2d2: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 7 — The moment Toh Ai Hwa takes her spot on stage in a Teochew iron-rod puppet performance, she will have to remain on stage for the next four hours even when heavily pregnant or sick.
The 76-year-old said her son was almost due for delivery when the troupe leader told her to join a performance in Bukit Mertajam.

“I asked him what if I went into labour and he told me if I go into labour, they will send me to the hospital and it happened that just as the show ended, I went into labour so I dropped the instruments and they took me to the hospital,” she said.
She said there was no such thing as maternity leave during that era so she had worked throughout her pregnancies.
She recounted another time when she had to perform at a temple on a hill and she had to ride pillion on a motorcycle up the hill while pregnant with another child.

“At that time, I asked my boss what will happen if I go into labour on the hill top so he brought a midwife along as a precaution,” she said, adding that fortunately, she did not go into labour on the hill and only delivered a few days later.
Toh said this is the life of performers that were often dictated by the schedules of their shows as her mother was also pregnant with her when performing in a Chinese Opera.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Teochew iron-rod puppeteer Toh Ai Hwa was honoured for her achievement as a recipient of the Living National Heritage Award. From left: Ling Goh, National Heritage Department director general Mohamad Muda Bahadin, Toh and state exco Wong Hon Wai. — Picture by Opalyn Mok
“My mother, who came from China, was a traditional Opera performer here in Penang so she went into labour in the midst of a performance,” she said.
Toh said she came from a long line of performers as her grandmother was also a traditional Opera singer in China and all of her family members have deep interest in performing arts.
She has been in the Teochew iron-rod puppetry field for 64 years, performing even when she was ill and bringing her children and, later, grandchildren along to shows.
“Once, I was so sick, I can only lie down to play the gong and drum during a performance because the show must go on,” she said.
She had taken an apprenticeship in Teochew puppetry at the age of 12 due to her interest in singing and performing.

“It was the 1950s, there were hardly any jobs, I was not educated as my mother didn’t believe girls should go to school, so when I chanced upon the puppetry troupe, I joined them and started learning from the troupe leader,” she said.
She said all apprentices have to learn the art of puppetry first before learning the music and singing.
“The iron-rod wooden puppets were so heavy so I decided to focus on playing the gong and drum, and the singing since I loved to sing,” she said.
When her boss wanted to retire, she said he offered to sell the troupe to her and that was when she took over the Kim Giak Low Choon Teochew Puppet Troupe in 1989.
It was not an easy path to follow in preserving the puppetry tradition as she said at one point, there were hardly any bookings for their performances.
“Sometimes, we only have bookings of one or two performances a month or during some festivals, it was a challenge to earn a living at that time,” she said.
Despite that, she ensured that all four of her children learnt the trade from her so all of them has the skills for puppetry along with playing the gong and drum music.
She said her sister was also a puppeteer and her brother, who was a traditional Opera performer, eventually learnt puppetry from her and set up his own troupe.

“Now, puppetry performances are gaining popularity so there are also other troupes but there was a period when my troupe was the only one in the country because income was low and no one was interested in learning it,” she said.
To ensure continuity of the traditional puppetry performance, Toh said her grandchildren grew up learning the art of puppetry.
One of them is her oldest granddaughter, Goh Sin Ee, 25, who is part of the Gaik Lai Teochew Puppet Show troupe.
Growing up around the troupe, she learnt first how to handle the puppets and later how to sing.
“I have a day job in a factory in Bayan Lepas but after working hours, I spend my time in my family’s puppetry performances,” she said.
She said her younger sister is a full-time performer while her younger brother is a student who is also involved in the troupe.
“All of us learnt the trade from young and all of us can perform, we feel it is important to preserve this family tradition and culture,” she said.
She said the troupe often gets bookings for performances during specific celebrations and festivals such as deities’ birthdays, the Hungry Ghost Month and during the Nine Emperor Gods Festival.
Toh hopes that her grandchildren will continue to pass down the family tradition and culture to their children and grandchildren.
“I hope we can continue this down to the sixth generation or more,” she said.

Apart from the WAKOH recognition, Toh also received the Living Heritage Treasure of Penang award in 2008, a recognition for her lifetime contribution from George Town World Heritage Incorporated in 2020, and the Penang State Arts Icon Award in 2025.

Toh’s Teochew iron-rod puppetry performance was also among 10 traditional trades featured in Penang Global Tourism’s traditional trades campaign this year, held in collaboration with Penang Heritage Trust.
87bb01028e5b7aaa: TEHRAN, Nov 7 — Iran’s Armed Forces have control over the Strait of Hormuz, which will remain closed until the United States accepts Tehran’s conditions, Army spokesperson Brigadier General Mohammad Akraminia said, the Islamic Republic News Agency (IRNA) reported.

Speaking Friday evening at a ceremony in Pishva County, Tehran Province, honouring commanders and pilots killed in the June 5, 1963, uprising, he said Iran’s Army, Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC) and Law Enforcement Command were better prepared after direct confrontation with the United States and the Israeli regime.
He said public support had boosted military morale.
Before the war, about 130 ships crossed the strait daily, carrying 20 per cent of global oil, plus jet fuel and chemical fertilisers.
Akraminia warned that renewed US aggression would prompt an immediate response.
American bases and interests in the Persian Gulf and beyond West Asia, he said, were within range of Iranian drones and missiles.
Forces would follow the order of the Leader of the Islamic Revolution, Ayatollah Sayyid Mojtaba Hosseini Khamenei, to respond swiftly, effectively and without geographic limits.
Citing US officials, Akraminia put Washington’s direct war costs at more than US$48 billion (RM196.8 billion), with indirect losses potentially lasting years.
The military official cited Republican election setbacks and protests in European countries.
He also said 251 nights of public solidarity gatherings had further strengthened national unity. — Bernama-IRNA
9c2c4a622604165e: KANGAR, Nov 7 — Universiti Islam Antarabangsa Tuanku Syed Sirajuddin (UniSIRAJ) graduates must be trustworthy and uphold integrity, respect differences and stand by the truth - qualities that should guide them as they embark on their careers and future lives.

Raja Muda of Perlis Tuanku Syed Faizuddin Putra Jamalullail, who is also UniSIRAJ Chancellor, said knowledge developed one’s ability to think and solve problems, while good manners reflected one’s values.
“Ensure that academic excellence and expertise are always accompanied by strong moral values and principles,” he said at the 9th UniSIRAJ Convocation Ceremony at Dewan 2020 here today.
Tuanku Syed Faizuddin Putra said that in an era of artificial intelligence (AI) and digital advancement, the pursuit of knowledge must always go hand in hand with noble values and strong principles.

He also said graduates should build their careers diligently, discharge their responsibilities well and leverage their expertise to generate ideas and solutions that would add value to organisations and society.
“Success is not merely about positions, income or personal achievements, but also about the benefits one brings to others. The journey after convocation will not necessarily be easy.

“Failures, competition and changes will test one’s abilities. Turn every challenge into an opportunity to learn, address weaknesses and improve one’s capabilities. Face them with patience, perseverance and faith in Allah, without compromising one’s principles or self-respect,” he said.

Meanwhile, he said knowledge and expertise must translate into actions that bring benefits to others. Those who become leaders should lead with integrity, educators should teach with a strong sense of responsibility, while professionals should carry out their duties conscientiously and prioritise the interests of humanity.
Tuanku Syed Faizuddin Putra said every position and opportunity should be regarded as a platform to serve others.

At the convocation ceremony, the Raja Muda of Perlis also presented the Chancellor’s Award (Martabat Al-Syaraf Al-Ula) to Maryam Al Adzra Mohd Zawawi, a Bachelor of Hadith graduate from the Faculty of Al-Quran and Sunnah, who achieved a cumulative grade point average (CGPA) of 3.95.
A total of 277 UniSIRAJ graduates received their respective Doctor of Philosophy (PhD), Master’s, Bachelor’s and Diploma scrolls at the ceremony. — Bernama

dc452e874e0a2436: MELAKA: Umno Youth will lodge police reports over the delay in implementing the house arrest order involving former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak.

Its chief, Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh, said the reports, to be lodged at state and divisional levels, would enable the authorities to investigate whether there had been any breach of the law in implementing the royal decree and court order.
He said Umno Youth was also calling for the immediate implementation of the decree by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong allowing Najib to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest.
"Umno Youth calls for the immediate implementation of His Majesty's decree and for Najib to be allowed to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest.
"Any further proceedings, including a referral to the court, should not be used as a reason to delay the implementation of a decree that His Majesty has declared to be clear and unambiguous.

"As decreed by His Majesty, the power of pardon is a Royal Prerogative under Article 42 of the Federal Constitution, and its implementation must be respected in accordance with the position of the Constitutional Monarchy and the principle of the rule of law," he said in a statement shared on his Facebook page.
The Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) said today that seeking a court ruling on Najib's house arrest did not override the King's power to grant pardons.
It said the King's constitutional authority to grant pardons and the courts' power to interpret the legal effect of an order were separate matters.

9318d23f7ce3137d: PUTRAJAYA: The Gig Workers Tribunal has ruled on three disputes involving e-hailing drivers and an e-hailing platform operator, including upholding the deactivation of a driver's account for misconduct.
The human resources ministry said the three cases involved financial claims, the handling of digital platform systems, and the deactivation of a driver's account by GrabCar Sdn Bhd.

The ministry said the tribunal, presided over by its deputy president, Suzarika Sahak, partially upheld an e-hailing driver's financial claim against GrabCar in the first case, involving earnings from Saver bookings and the Cashback and Advance Booking incentive.
The driver was awarded RM2,000 in compensation.

In the second case, involving seven non-financial claims against GrabCar, the tribunal found three breaches of the Gig Workers Act 2025 relating to temporary booking pauses, booking cancellation quotas, and the Auto Accept system.

In both cases, the tribunal recommended improvements under Subsection 42(3) of Act 872, including ensuring drivers are informed of the type of service and earnings before accepting a booking, and given a reasonable and safe window to cancel.

In the third case, the tribunal upheld GrabCar's decision to permanently deactivate a driver's account after finding evidence of three incidents of misconduct towards passengers, involving inappropriate conversations, intimidating or threatening behaviour, and unwarranted personal questions.
"Although the deactivation of an account may affect a driver's livelihood, the tribunal held that passenger safety and wellbeing must not be compromised," the ministry said in a statement.
It said the decisions reflected the tribunal's balanced approach to upholding gig workers' rights, ensuring passenger safety, and protecting the interests of e-hailing platform operators.
e60a27ab7b6ac466: A roadside display at Cherwell Valley services has stopped dispensing information and started asking for help.

The eagle-eyed Register reader who spotted the stricken screen told us: "UK motorway signs often tell us that tiredness can kill, urging us to take a break. This poor thing at Cherwell Valley services took the advice to heart."

The display at the Moto services appears to have run into trouble during a restart. Windows offers another attempt or access to repair tools, although the latter options are hidden – perhaps somewhere on the top floor of the neighboring Travelodge. Getting things moving again will probably require access to the computer behind the screen.

The Automatic Repair screen is all too familiar to Windows users. Not to be confused with the classic blue screen of death, it might indicate a misbehaving driver during a reboot, an update that did something unexpected, or some sort of hardware failure. Hopefully it isn't the latter – with memory and storage prices the way they are at the moment, a motorway services sandwich or gallon of fuel will seem a positive bargain by comparison.
Our reader is right: taking a break is sensible advice. Getting Windows to end one can be another matter. ®
c65e697062f250d0: KUALA LUMPUR: World No. 9 men's doubles pair Man Wei Chong-Tee Kai Wun have set their sights on breaking into the world's top eight ahead of next year's Malaysia Open after conceding that their hopes of qualifying for the World Tour Finals are all but over.

The French Open champions revealed their ambition following a 21-17, 21-17 semi-final defeat to South Korea's world No. 1 Kim Won Ho-Seo Seung Jae at the Korea Open at Jinnam Stadium in Yeosu on Saturday.

Wei Chong said the pair would now focus on making the most of their remaining two tournaments, the Kumamoto Masters beginning on Tuesday and the Hong Kong Open, before turning their attention to the new season.

"I think we can't qualify for the World Tour Finals, and we just want to play our best in the next two tournaments, and maybe our target is top eight for next year's Malaysia Open," said Wei Chong in a post-match interview with the Badminton World Federation.
The defeat also extended Wei Chong-Kai Wun's miserable record against Won Ho-Seung Jae, who have now beaten the Malaysians in all seven of their meetings.
Despite arriving in Yeosu after their French Open Super 750 triumph last month, Wei Chong-Kai Wun once again found themselves unable to overcome the formidable Koreans.
The Malaysians remained competitive throughout the 39-minute encounter but struggled to contain their opponents' attacking play at crucial moments.
There was also a moment of controversy late in the opening game when Won Ho swung at a shuttle that appeared to be heading out with the Koreans leading 18-17.
His racket slipped from his hand and struck the net, prompting Kai Wun to appeal for a fault, but the umpire waved away his protest.
The Malaysians then challenged the line call unsuccessfully, allowing Won Ho-Seung Jae to establish a two-point advantage at 19-17 before closing out the game.
Wei Chong admitted their defensive shortcomings made it hard to withstand the Koreans' relentless attacking pressure.
"I think for me, my defence today was not really good because I couldn't return a few of their smashes. So, I think that's the problem," said Wei Chong.
Kai Wun echoed his partner's assessment, explaining that their struggles in defence had also affected their tactical approach.
"Because our defence was not doing really well, we didn't want to lift so easily, and from there we didn't do so well," said Kai Wun.
Despite the setback, Kai Wun believes the pair have improved significantly since last season, although recurring weaknesses continue to keep them from performing consistently at the highest level.
"I think actually it's already getting better compared with last year, but we still have things to learn because there are still small issues that we need to work on," he said.

b6ca0674f6a54057: KUALA LUMPUR: Inspired by legendary track cyclist Azizulhasni Awang, national sailor Khairulnizam Afendy is determined to make his fifth Olympic appearance at the 2028 Los Angeles games.
A career-threatening spine injury, which left him struggling to walk, saw Khairulnizam going under the surgeon's knife in January.
He has made positive strides since making his comeback recently, which includes winning an ILCA 7 (formerly known as laser standard) bronze at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games last month.
Khairulnizam, who suffered from three herniated discs, said his condition has improved since the operation though is not quite pain-free.

"One of the discs (L5 S1) was compressing my nerve and I almost could not walk at the time, so I had to go for arthroscopic surgery (microdiscectomy) to trim that disc as soon as possible," said Khairulnizam.
"My condition has improved since then but I still have two more bad discs which I have to manage carefully.
"These kinds of injuries are pretty common in sailing due to the nature of the sport as well as the heavy work we do in the gym.
"I took a six-month break after the operation and only had about two or three months to prepare for the Asian Games so I was very grateful to win a medal."
The injury setbacks have not diminished his desire to compete in a fifth Olympics. He has not missed an edition since making his debut at London 2012.
Khairulnizam, 33, said Azizulhasni's decision to continue racing until LA 2028 has fired him up.
"Datuk Azizulhasni has also come back for LA 2028. I consider him my idol as I am younger than him," he said.
"If he can do it, then why can't I? We should accept the challenge and try to emulate the immense fighting spirit he has.
"I also want to compete at LA 2028 and do better than I did before. I believe my chances of qualifying are positive."
Azizulhasni, a two-time Olympic medallist, is no stranger to adversity himself. In early 2022, he underwent open-heart surgery to correct a coronary artery anomaly he suffered from since birth.
Despite his advancing years, the 38-year-old has enjoyed the strongest season of his career this year.
He emerged the overall keirin champion in the UCI World Cup series and won the keirin gold at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games as well as keirin gold and individual sprint bronze at the Asian Games.
Khairulnizam's next major assignment will be the world championships in Fortaleza, Brazil (Jan 15-23) which will also serve as an Olympic qualifier.
Finishing in the top-16 will earn him an automatic berth at LA 2028.

c34c8f0f1a945051: KUALA LUMPUR: The recent disruption affecting several bank websites was believed to have occurred amid a surge in cyberattacks targeting Malaysia's telecommunications and banking infrastructure.

He added that Japan had previously recorded simultaneous attacks on 128 banks, causing severe system disruptions.
"There were also disruptions affecting several banks in Malaysia. However, we observed the swift action taken by our banking sector, with systems restored to normal within a short period," he said.
Siraj said the National Cyber Security Agency's move to raise the country's cybersecurity threat level from low to moderate underscored the need for greater preparedness.
He said the impact of an attack depended on an institution's level of readiness, including workforce capability, hardware and security systems.

"Disruptions to critical infrastructure do not only affect banking operations, but can also impact telecommunications, transportation and aviation services, causing difficulties in daily public affairs.

"The priority now is to ensure any intrusion is detected and addressed rapidly to prevent prolonged damage and service disruptions, thereby safeguarding the security of the nation's critical infrastructure," he said.

Meanwhile, cybersecurity expert and former CyberSecurity Malaysia (CSM) chief executive officer Datuk Dr Amirudin Abdul Wahab did not rule out the possibility of cyberattacks, particularly following reports of intrusions and the defacement of banking websites.

"The most critical task now is determining whether these incidents only involve customer-facing websites and access systems, or if they have compromised core banking systems, customer databases and financial transaction infrastructure.
"We must also confirm if there are customer data leaks or unauthorised transactions. This can only be determined through comprehensive digital forensic investigations," he said.

37306f0f384233db: ASUNCION (Paraguay), Nov 7 — Pedro Alliana became president of Paraguay on Friday following the impeachment of his predecessor over a massive banking crisis that locked almost half the country out of their accounts.
Senators appointed Alliana, the former vice president, shortly after voting to remove Santiago Pena over the chaotic collapse of a bank to which he had links.
Senate President Basilio Nunez declared Pena “guilty of poor performance in his duties” after 44 out of 45 senators voted in favor of impeachment, with one lawmaker absent.
Hundreds of people waiting outside Congress raucously celebrated his impeachment.
“Justice has been done. Now we want him to give us back our money and go to jail,” Jessica Aquino, 32, told AFP.
Paraguayan authorities placed the ex-leader under house arrest minutes after his removal, prosecutor Silvia Margarita Gonzalez Vester told reporters.
Alliana promised not to abandon the almost three million depositors, including pensioners, affected by Ueno Bank’s takeover amid insolvency concerns.
“Compatriots who are now going through a difficult time as a result of the financial collapse will be fully compensated,” said Alliana, who will serve as president until 2028.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Paraguay’s Vice-President Pedro Alliana (centre) takes the oath of office as interim president at Congress in Asuncion on November 6, 2026, after the impeachment of Santiago Pena over a banking crisis. — AFP pic
Opposition lawmakers had also filed a motion to impeach Alliana over the crisis, but the request failed to gain congressional approval.
Money trickles back
The bank’s demise brought thousands of people onto the streets demanding repercussions for US-backed Pena, who until last year had a stake in Grupo Vazquez, which controlled Ueno.
Advance payments to an unspecified number of impacted depositors began on Thursday afternoon, a Central Bank official told AFP.

The first phase of aid deposits, up to around US$1,600 (RM6,560), will go to clients who don’t have loans and have an account at another bank or institution in Paraguay to receive the funds, said Jose Maciel of the Central Bank’s Deposit Guarantee Fund.
The next beneficiaries “will be announced progressively over the course of the payment process,” he added.
Pena had offered his resignation over the disaster, but lawmakers pressed ahead with impeachment proceedings that have stripped him of political immunity.
The opposition accused the US-backed politician of a conflict of interest, which he denied.
The Attorney General said it was investigating him for “acts related to the supervision and resolution of Ueno Bank S.A. and the placement of public funds in said entity.”
He will be questioned over alleged crimes of breach of trust, influence peddling, and misappropriation of funds on Saturday, prosecutor Gonzalez Vester said.
Pena urged reconciliation in an X post shortly before his removal.
“Today, we must come together as Paraguayans to rebuild our institutions and restore trust,” he said.
The US Embassy in Paraguay expressed “its solidarity with the Paraguayan people” on Friday, without mentioning the president.
‘Pena in prison’
“Pena in prison,” read one of the protest signs outside Congress on Friday.
On Thursday, thousands demonstrated for a third consecutive night in Asuncion and other cities to demand the return of their money.

“Santiago Pena has hurt so many Paraguayans, so many families, business owners and small business people, including my own son, who had savings in Ueno Bank,” Cynthia Farina told AFP at a protest in the capital that police dispersed with tear gas and water cannons.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Police special forces officers stand guard outside a Ueno Bank branch covered with banners and graffiti in downtown Asuncion on November 6, 2026, after the bank’s collapse locked thousands out of their savings. — AFP pic

Ueno began as a small fintech company with a digital-first model that attracted low-income customers, rapidly becoming a major bank that handled state pensions and the accounts of several state entities.
The scandal has claimed the heads of Central Bank President Carlos Carvallo and Interior Minister Enrique Riera, while eight Ueno executives have been arrested.
Police conducted raids on various locations linked to Grupo Vazquez on Wednesday and Thursday.
Nearby Argentina felt the impact of the crisis as some 1,000 employees of technology company ITTI, which is part of Grupo Vazquez, were suspended for 30 days without pay.
Football also took a hit.
Ueno Bank sponsors several first division teams as well as the national team.
“We were also victims of this situation,” members of the national team said in a statement on X. — AFP
57b9d6362f0d80bf: And helping to make the goals for EU accession plausible
Originally published on Global Voices
Screenshot from the EkoMapa website of the EkoGard organization in Montenegro. Fair use.

This interview is part of a series of spotlights on the work of some of the grantees of the Digital Spark granting scheme, as part of the Regional Support Mechanism EECA project, implemented by the Metamorphosis Foundation and TechSoup, in partnership with CIVICUS and under the Digital Democracy Initiative (DDI) that covers the Global South. It is being published on Global Voices as part of a content-sharing agreement.

Montenegro is on its way to joining the EU; at the moment, the goal is to do so by 2028. The United Nations Economic Commission for Europe (UNECE) review in 2025 states that the country has made significant progress in aligning its environmental legal and regulatory framework, as well as much of its national legislation, with European Union (EU) directives.
However, some problems remain, including waste management and a very low recycling rate — less than 2 percent, far below the EU’s 50 percent target.

Austrian Member of Parliament Thomas Waitz (Greens/EFA), chair of the delegation to the EU-Montenegro Stabilisation and Association Parliamentary Committee, said in an interview with The New Union Post that there have been “massive improvements” in Montenegro, citing as an example the closure of more than 100 illegal landfills in the last year: “It is a great effort for such a small country. But they have another 500, and if we expected them to have them all cleaned up, it would be impossible.”

While politicians and international agencies discuss how Montenegro could get closer to the target and put its waste management under control, ordinary citizens are making practical steps to improve the situation today.
This Digital Spark spotlight story is about one such organization, EkoGard, and the many people who participate in its efforts and, step by step, try to make Montenegro cleaner.
Global Voices interviewed the organization’s founder and general director, Senad Pepić, about the impact of Digital Spark and its community initiative.
Global Voices (GV): Please tell us about your organization and why you chose to get involved with the Digital Spark project.

Senad Pepić (SP): EkoGard was built through years of work on the ground, not in an office. It grew out of the Očistimo Rožaje initiative, where we spent six years building a strong community of people ready to take action. We started with illegal dumpsites, but our work gradually expanded to other environmental and social issues affecting everyday life.
We organized cleanups, worked with young people, launched campaigns, and encouraged residents to tackle problems that kept coming back.

We joined Digital Spark because we wanted to bring what we learned in the field together with digital tools and data. We hoped to show a fuller picture of the problems and change how people talk about them. EkoMapa grew out of that idea as a natural next step in our work.
GV: What issue or challenge in your community prompted you to undertake this project?

SP: One cleanup in particular made us rethink our approach. We cleared an illegal dumpsite beside a rural road, in an area where residents had no suitable place to dispose of their waste. The nearest legal disposal point was about six kilometers away.

After the cleanup, we asked for a waste container to be installed and were promised that the problem would be addressed. Three years passed; the container was never installed, and the dumpsite returned.

Its return changed how we saw similar sites elsewhere. We had photos, posts, and letters from other areas, but no way to see the full extent of the problem or how it related to gaps in waste collection services.

We wanted to map these places and understand the conditions in each settlement. Doing that gives us a way to show local institutions where waste disposal services are lacking and talk about what needs to change.
GV: What are the key changes or activities that your organization implemented during your participation in the project?

SP: Before this project, EkoGard organized cleanups, worked with young people, held educational activities, ran campaigns, and drew attention to local problems. Through Digital Spark, we began collecting and analysing what we saw in the field more systematically.

EkoMapa started as a map of illegal dumpsites, but it grew into a tool for understanding environmental conditions across the community. We decided to look at conditions settlement by settlement, so we could connect the problems we found with the services available to residents.

We also developed a model that uses the information we collect to assess environmental risks and gaps in local services in each settlement. It helps us spot patterns, compare needs across settlements, and discuss what the data shows with local institutions.
GV: How did your participation in the project impact your organization’s beneficiaries and the community that you serve? Please provide examples.
SP: Our activists now have a practical tool and a clearer way to document what they find. We can use that information in public campaigns and make a stronger case for change.
For residents, we can now show how the problems they face relate to the services available in their settlements.
Organizations from other towns and countries have also shown interest in using the tool to understand conditions in their own communities and involve residents in finding solutions.

The local waste management company has also recognized that the information could be useful in its work. For now, the clearest changes are in how our activists work and in the conversations we have begun with other organizations and local institutions. Changes on the ground will take longer.
GV: How has your own knowledge, awareness, and experience with digital democracy and civic space changed, thanks to your participation in the project?

SP: Through the project, we learned that giving people a way to report a problem is only a first step. They also need to know why we collect the information, what we will do with it, and how it might lead to change.
The training on how to reach people and communicate more clearly was especially useful. It made us think about the words we use and how to talk about problems without making people feel powerless.

For us, digital democracy means residents can help identify problems and take part in finding solutions. When we collect, check, and present what they tell us clearly, it can inform our campaigns and conversations with institutions. It also helps us ask for clearer answers.
GV: What are the most valuable lessons and experiences you are taking away from this project?

SP: The most valuable lesson is that technology cannot solve a problem on its own. It can help us see what is happening across a community, but it cannot replace fieldwork, talking with residents, or working with institutions.
Finding a problem on a map is just the beginning. We also need to understand why it happened. If we only deal with what we can see, the same problem is likely to return.

When we bring the data together with people’s experiences, we can start to propose solutions that meet their needs. That is what we will take into our future work: listen, look for patterns and causes, and use what we learn to push for change.
GV: What comes next? How will you apply the learning and digital capacity you have built in your future work and within your community?

SP: Our next step is to present our findings to the local government and make the case for better planning of waste collection and other local services. We want to draw attention to settlements that have been overlooked for years and follow up on how institutions respond.

We are already applying what we learned to EkoGard’s wider work, especially our campaigns and how we involve residents. Together with other organizations from Montenegro, we are preparing a campaign to establish a National Eco Line, a nationwide channel for reporting environmental problems and following up on how the responsible authorities respond.
We know the results may take time, so we will keep working with other organizations and local institutions.
Written by Daria Dergacheva

c65367e3aa20f04d: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — Several Umno leaders in Johor have lodged a police report over the delay in implementing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s house arrest, as Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhammad Akmal Saleh called for similar reports to be filed nationwide.

Pontian Umno chief Datuk Seri Ahmad Maslan, who is also a party supreme council member, lodged the report at the Benut police station at 12.30pm today, accompanied by his deputy Mohd Sumali Reduan, division vice-chief Jamaludin Abd Majid and several grassroots leaders.
“A police report was lodged over the delay in implementing the house arrest order for Najib, which should have been carried out,” Ahmad said in a Facebook post.

Meanwhile, Dr Akmal said Umno Youth branches at state and division levels would lodge police reports to seek an investigation into whether any laws had been breached in delaying the implementation of the royal pardon and related court order.
In a statement today, he urged the government to immediately implement the conditional pardon granted by His Majesty, Sultan Ibrahim, maintaining that all stipulated conditions had been fulfilled.

“On November 6, all conditions were met. The RM50 million fine was paid at the Kuala Lumpur High Court, which then issued a sealed order allowing Datuk Seri Najib to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest. He argued that further legal proceedings should not delay the implementation of the order.

“Umno Youth demands that His Majesty’s decree be implemented immediately. Any further court reference should not be used as grounds to stall a decree that His Majesty has confirmed to be clear and unambiguous,” he said.

It said the interpretation could affect when Najib’s separate prison sentence in the 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) case should begin.

In a further statement today, the AGC denied attempting to override the King’s authority, maintaining that judicial clarification was necessary to prevent conflicting interpretations of the court orders and ensure their lawful implementation.
Istana Negara, meanwhile, reaffirmed today that the conditional pardon granted on September 18 was clear and unambiguous, and that all stipulated conditions had been fulfilled.

The pardon allows Najib to serve the remainder of his SRC International sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, subject to payment of the RM50 million fine and compliance with other conditions.
Najib has been imprisoned since August 2022 following his conviction over the misappropriation of RM42 million in SRC International funds.

Residents along the route chipped in money towards the convoy’s travel costs and complained about the cost of living, The Thaiger reported.
Some said the fuel needed just to get to work was eating up their income.

Prayoon Changjai, who owns a large fish pier in Pathio district and runs boats on fuel, told reporters coconuts had sold for about 2 baht (RM0.24) each for nearly 30 years and were still hard to sell, The Thaiger reported.
She said fuel and other costs kept climbing even as fuel prices abroad fell, and that the prime minister should step down if he could not fix the problem.
Bangkok’s Metropolitan Police Bureau commissioner, Police Lieutenant General Siam Boonsom, has banned public gatherings within 50 metres of Government House until midnight on November 20.
The order cites risks to traffic, access to Government House and public safety, and names the alliance’s planned rally as the reason, according to the report.
MGR Online’s report on the order mentioned no road closures.
It is not clear how many vehicles will reach Bangkok, as the group had aimed for 1,000 cars and trucks.
The Thai Examiner reported that Mano admitted turnout was below that target.
The government has issued no public statement on the 10-baht (RM1.22) demand as of the time of publishing, according to The Thaiger.

PTT, Thailand’s state-controlled oil and gas company, sold regular diesel at 41.79 baht (RM5.10) a litre and B20 diesel, a blend with 20 per cent biodiesel, at 33.50 baht (RM4.09) a litre on November 7, according to a daily price list published by Thairath, a leading Thai newspaper, that excludes local taxes.

Since November 1, the Oil Fuel Fund, a government-run fund that cushions fuel prices, has paid a subsidy of 3.90 baht (RM0.48) a litre on regular diesel and 5.82 baht (RM0.71) on B20, under new rates set at the end of October, The Thaiger reported.
6e611d0a2fb341a4: MEXICO CITY: Mexican police shot dead a seven-year-old American girl when they opened fire on her family's vehicle from a helicopter during a drug enforcement operation, the state prosecutor confirmed Friday.

f3f69b602f68f8e2: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 7 — The Gig Workers Tribunal (TPG) has ruled on three disputes involving e-hailing drivers and GrabCar Sdn Bhd, including awarding RM2,000 in compensation to one driver while upholding the deactivation of another driver’s account over misconduct involving passengers.

The Human Resources Ministry (Kesuma) said in a statement today that the three cases involved financial claims, the handling of digital platform systems and the deactivation of a driver’s account, which TPG deputy president Suzarika Sahak heard.

According to Kesuma, the tribunal partially upheld an e-hailing driver’s financial claim against GrabCar in the first case, involving earnings from Saver bookings and the ‘Cashback and Advance Booking’ incentive.
“The tribunal also awarded RM2,000 in compensation, together with interest at eight per cent per annum until full settlement.

“The tribunal also found that GrabCar’s use of the ‘Auto Accept’ and ‘Fast Cancel’ mechanisms on its digital platform violated Section 8(1)(b) and (c) of the Gig Workers Act 2025 (Act 872),” the ministry said, noting that the provisions safeguard gig workers’ right to know the type of service and the agreed payment before accepting a job.
In the second case, another e-hailing driver brought seven non-financial claims against GrabCar over how it handled and operated its digital platform.

“The tribunal found three breaches of Act 872, relating to temporary booking pauses, booking cancellation quotas and the ‘Auto Accept’ system,” it said, adding that the temporary suspension of bookings and the platform’s failure to explain the terms and duration of the measure were found to contravene Section 8(1)(a) and Section 8(2)(a) and (b) of the Act.

“The tribunal also found that the failure to clearly explain how cancellation quotas are set, what happens when the quota is reached and the options for cancelling bookings for reasonable reasons violated Section 8(2)(a) and (b) of the Act,” it said.

The statement also said that the operation of the ‘Auto Accept’ system, which resulted in bookings being accepted before drivers were informed of the type of service and the earnings offered, was also found to breach Section 8(1)(b) and (c) of Act 872.

In both cases, the tribunal recommended improvements under Subsection 42(3) of Act 872, including ensuring drivers are informed of the type of service and earnings before accepting a booking and given a reasonable and safe window to cancel, Kesuma said.

“The tribunal further recommended clearer terms governing temporary booking pauses, cancellation quotas, incentive programmes and booking restrictions, as well as better access to platform support personnel and a human review process for decisions made by automated systems,” it said.

In the third case, the tribunal upheld GrabCar’s decision to permanently deactivate a driver’s account after finding evidence of three incidents of misconduct towards passengers, involving inappropriate conversations, intimidating or threatening behaviour, and unwarranted personal questions.

“Although the deactivation of an account may affect a driver’s livelihood, the tribunal held that passenger safety and well-being must not be compromised. The driver’s claim was therefore dismissed,” Kesuma said.

The ministry emphasised that the three decisions reflected the tribunal’s balanced approach to upholding gig workers’ rights, ensuring passenger safety and protecting the interests of e-hailing platform operators.

The ministry also pledged to strengthen enforcement of Act 872 through the TPG, an independent, fair and effective mechanism for resolving disputes, to support a more transparent, sustainable and accountable gig economy. — Bernama

7b6aa99d735ea5ae: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 7 — Traditional performance arts usually involves singing, acting and dancing but Universiti Sains Malaysia’s (USM) traditional performing arts master Adiguru Che Mat Jusoh hopes the younger generation will look into documenting traditional arts and culture to preserve intangible heritage.

Che Mat, who was awarded the Living National Heritage Award (WAKOH) this year by the Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture (Motac), said traditional arts are not limited to singing, acting and dancing.
“Writing related to traditional arts and culture must also be given serious attention,” he said in a statement issued by USM today.
He added that this aspect was still not given enough emphasis among the younger generation.
“Documentation and writing are important ways to ensure that the knowledge, history and philosophy of heritage were not lost to time,” he said.
Che Mat had spent nearly 58 years to preserving and sustaining the traditional performing arts of Mak Yong and Kelantanese Wayang Kulit.
The 72-year-old is not only a traditional arts practitioner but is also one of the key custodians of traditional knowledge, skills and musical repertoire inherited from earlier generations.
He said the prestigious award was not merely a personal achievement but also recognition of efforts to uphold a heritage that must be safeguarded.
“Of course, I am very happy that all the effort and commitment I have devoted over the years to preserving traditional arts have finally received the government’s attention and recognition,” he said.
Che Mat also said he was among those still able to play old Mak Yong songs that were increasingly being lost to time.
He added that he was proud that a younger generation was now showing interest in learning them.
“However, knowledge of traditional arts cannot be passed down in a hurry. It must be taught little by little, with patience and commitment, just as I learned it myself,” he said.
He said he wanted to ensure that traditional arts and heritage continued to thrive and does not stop with one generation.

“I want them to continue to live, grow and be passed on to future generations. Heritage should not merely be a memory or a relic of history; it must continue to be practised and strengthened,” he said.

Besides his contributions to traditional performing arts, Che Mat, who was previously a resident artist at USM, has also produced literary work with the publication of his latest book, Hikayat Maharaja Seri Rama, this year.

The book was published by Nusa Centre, which has published three of Che Mat’s major works with support from a MOTAC grant. The publication is also part of continuing efforts to preserve the country’s intangible cultural heritage.

The book, compiled by Che Mat, is an important effort to preserve and document a treasure of Malay literature that has developed within the cultural sphere of the Malay Archipelago for more than 1,000 years.
b18b169a1b15ae40: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — Bank Rakyat said today that a disruption to its corporate website was caused by a technical problem involving a third-party service provider, assuring customers that their deposits, personal information and banking services remained unaffected.

The bank advised customers to use alternative digital banking platforms but did not specify the cause of the disruption or indicate when access would be restored.

a401fb35218afa5e: BEIJING: Top officials from Washington and Beijing held "frank" talks on their countries' testy trade relationship on Friday, ahead of an Asia-Pacific summit in China this month where their leaders are due to meet.

Treasury secretary Scott Bessent and US trade representative Jamieson Greer held a call with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng and discussed economic and trade commitments over the last year, both sides said.

The Americans stressed "the importance of China fully and immediately implementing its commitments" and highlighted "concerns about recent Chinese actions", according to a statement released by the US Treasury Department.

China's He, meanwhile, expressed "serious concerns over recent economic and trade restrictive measures imposed by the United States", according to a state media report shared online by Beijing's commerce ministry on Saturday.
The report did not specify which measures He was referring to, but added that the talks were "frank, in-depth and constructive".
Bessent "underscored that continued progress depends on concrete results and that the US will closely assess China's implementation of the arrangement", said the Treasury.

The statement referenced China's commitments from an October 2025 meeting between presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in Busan, South Korea, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit.
China is hosting this year's Apec gathering from Nov 18 to 19 in Shenzhen, which could also see a trilateral meeting with Trump, Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Beijing's foreign ministry said this week it was in contact with Washington and Moscow about the possibility.

The Busan agreement, which reflected calming tensions between the superpowers after they had exchanged tariff escalations earlier in 2025, required China to purchase US soybeans this year and through 2028.
China also agreed to suspend new export controls on rare earths and to issue general licences for exports of the materials.
The accord initially covered one year, but the two sides extended the ceasefire through to Jan 10, 2027, during Xi's September visit to the White House.
Both sides agreed during Friday's call to "properly manage differences" and promote a "stable" US-China trade relationship, according to the Chinese commerce ministry's readout on Saturday.
In a separate statement, the ministry reiterated China's "firm" opposition to new US sanctions targeting Cuba, which affected two Chinese companies.
The statement from an unnamed spokesperson added that Washington's recent sanctions "escalation" against China ran counter to the consensus reached by Trump and Xi.
Trade experts have said one of the main sources of friction is over the level of Chinese rare-earth exports, which are crucial for the production of smartphones, automobiles and military equipment.
4c529e09e2a6980e: LOS ANGELES, Nov 7 — Need a guide for what to watch Apple TV in November? Here's a curated list.
Stick (Season Two) (Trailer here) — A feel-good sports comedy about second chances!

Stick is a sports comedy series created by Jason Keller and starring and executive produced by Owen Wilson. Wilson stars as Pryce Cahill, an over-the-hill, ex-pro golfer whose career was derailed prematurely 20 years ago. After the collapse of his marriage and while working at an Indiana sporting goods store, Pryce hedges his bets, and future, entirely on a troubled 17-year-old golf phenom named Santi (Peter Dager). Stick is a heartfelt, feel-good comedy about a found family and their relationships set within the world of golf as it has never been shown before.

Hollywood actor and comedian Nora Lum (aka Awkwafina) is the descendant of restaurant royalty … but she can’t cook. Join the star on an inspiring culinary road trip as she learns the craft and attempts to revive her family’s beloved Chinese eatery.

Each episode of 12 12 12 unfolds across three timelines of a heist: the 12 months of planning, the 12 hours of the heist and the 12 days following it. The series follows a disgraced FBI agent (Anthony Mackie) and an American career criminal (Jamie Dornan) as they play a zero-sum game of cat and mouse across Europe. At the center of it all is the daring, epic raid on a bank vault deep beneath the streets of Zurich.

They wouldn’t take Judy Heumann’s phone calls, so she took their building. In 1977, a young disabled woman (Ruth Madeley) and a scrappy coalition of outsiders decide they’ve had enough. What begins as one impulsive act becomes the longest occupation of a federal building in American history, as hundreds spontaneously seize government offices and refuse to leave until the bureaucrat in their way (Mark Ruffalo) takes action. Bringing rebellion in all its forms to the hallowed halls, a movement’s accidental leaders struggle to find their path forward where none has ever been paved for them. Directed by Academy Award winner Siân Heder (“CODA”) and based on true events, Being Heumann is the revolutionary, irreverent and deeply human story of the least likely people trying to pull off the impossible and change the lives of millions.
Way of the Warrior Kid (Trailer here)

Middle school has been a nightmare for Marc (Jude Hill), a good kid who’s bullied by his classmates and feels like he’s behind in everything, from academics to P.E. to just making friends. That changes when his injured Uncle Jake (Chris Pratt), a decorated Navy SEAL, comes to spend the summer and recuperate with Marc and his mom, Sarah (Linda Cardellini). To help Marc defend himself, Jake devises an ambitious program he calls “Operation Warrior Kid” based on his SEAL training. Instead of teaching his nephew how to fight, Jake shows Marc what real courage is, facing down his own demons along the way. Based on the bestselling novel by former Navy SEAL Jocko Willink, “Way of the Warrior Kid” is directed by McG (Charlie’s Angels, Terminator Salvation) from a screenplay by Will Staples (Without Remorse, The Right Stuff).
The following titles will have all episodes available to binge-watch this November.

This darkly funny espionage drama follows a team of British intelligence agents who serve in a dumping ground department of MI5 due to their career-ending mistakes. Led by their brilliant but irascible leader, the notorious Jackson Lamb (Academy Award winner Sir Gary Oldman), they navigate the espionage world’s smoke and mirrors to defend England from sinister forces.

Hailed as one of the best sci-fi novels and celebrating the 10th anniversary of its release this year, “Dark Matter” is a story about the road not taken. In season one, the series followed Jason Dessen (Joel Edgerton), a physicist, professor and family man who — one night while walking home on the streets of Chicago — is abducted into an alternate version of his life. Wonder quickly turns to nightmare when he tries to return to his reality amid the mind-bending landscape of lives he could have lived. Season two picks up with the Dessens as they settle into a quiet life in a world that finally seems safe until the unimaginable forces them to run once again. As Jason’s obsession with the Box deepens, Daniela’s (Jennifer Connelly) growing paranoia pushes her to the brink, threatening to tear their fragile stability apart. Elsewhere, Amanda (Alice Braga) and Ryan (Jimmi Simpson) join forces in a desperate attempt to find their way home. With Blair (Amanda Brugel) determined to stop him, Leighton (Dayo Okeniyi) relentlessly chases his grand vision of creating a perfect world.

Brothers follows McConaughey and Harrelson, who play fictionalised versions of themselves, and whose lifelong friendship is thrown into chaos when they uncover a decades-old secret: they might actually be brothers. After Woody’s daughter’s wedding falls apart, he loads up the family and heads to Austin for an extended stay at Matthew’s ranch. But what begins as a healing getaway quickly spirals when Matthew’s mother, Ma Mac (played by Holland Taylor), accidentally lets slip a long-buried secret that the two friends might actually be brothers. As Woody turns the ranch upside down in pursuit of the truth, Matthew finds himself juggling an entirely different identity crisis: a potential run for Governor of Texas. The result is a heartfelt, chaotic and wildly funny story about friendship, family, fame and the messy line between myth and reality.
Knife Edge: Chasing Michelin Stars (Season Two)
Witness thrilling highs and crushing lows as expert chefs pursue the ultimate award: a Michelin Star. Get unprecedented insight into the secretive judging process.
1a0e2c00e6fe333f: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 7 — The Penang State Government is committed to ensuring that all 28 Sekolah Jenis Kebangsaan Tamil (SJKT) in the state secure their respective land titles, as part of efforts to strengthen educational facilities.
Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said as of June, land titles had been successfully secured for five schools, with plans to secure titles for another five within the next two to three years.
“In its efforts to strengthen educational facilities, the state government is also committed to ensuring that all 28 SJKT in Penang secure their respective land titles.

“One of the commitments fulfilled by the state government is the provision of a 2.368-acre site for the relocation project of SJKT Rajaji in Air Itam,” he said in a message delivered in conjunction with the Deepavali 2026 celebrations today.

Chow noted that the state government is also focusing on the development of Tamil-medium education, including initiatives to enhance digital skills and broaden students’ exposure to the fields of Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM).

Chow mentioned that in April, a total of RM2.42 million was allocated for the development of Tamil-medium schools in Penang. Of this amount, RM1.34 million was channelled through the Penang Education Council (PEC) to strengthen digital infrastructure and STEM competencies.

He added that RM768,901 was distributed to the 28 SJKTs via their respective Parent-Teacher Associations (PIBG) for the maintenance and improvement of learning facilities while RM194,400 was allocated to 11 kindergartens located within SJKT premises to support early childhood education.

Furthermore, Chow emphasised that educational progress must go hand in hand with efforts to preserve language and culture citing, for instance, the ‘Free Tamil Language Class’ initiative organised by the Village Community Management Council (MPKK) of Lebuh Pasar.
He expressed hope that more such initiatives would be implemented to ensure that linguistic and cultural heritage continues to be preserved among the younger generation.

Meanwhile, Chow said the state government will continue to collaborate with the federal government, educational institutions, civil society organisations, and the private sector to expand opportunities for inclusive development through the Madani Budget. 2027.

He said these efforts include support through the National Entrepreneur Group Economic Fund (Tekun Nasional), Amanah Ikhtiar Malaysia (AIM), and the Malaysian Indian Community Transformation Unit (Mitra), specifically aimed at empowering small-scale entrepreneurs and youths of Indian descent.
“Indeed, meaningful development is one which creates opportunities, enhances well-being, and ensures that every community can enjoy the benefits of the state’s progress,” he said.
He also expressed hope that this year’s Deepavali celebration would foster a spirit of goodwill and strengthen societal unity for the sake of a better future for Penang.
He added that the diversity of races, religions, languages, and cultures in Penang serves as a strength that unites the community in building a shared future. — Bernama

a3142a876b1fafaf: SEREMBAN, Nov 7 — Negeri Sembilan Umno chief Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias has denied plotting to oust Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim, dismissing speculation that a vote of no confidence was being planned amid uncertainty over the state’s political leadership.
Jalaluddin said no such move had been discussed at a meeting of the state Umno leadership today, insisting that claims of rival factions within the party were unfounded.
According to Utusan Malaysia, Jalaluddin was speaking after a Negeri Sembilan Umno liaison committee meeting at Wisma Umno in Seremban today.
“Have you heard me say I want to bring down the menteri besar? No. I made that clear at the meeting earlier.

“Even this morning, there were still claims that we would decide on a vote of no confidence against the menteri besar today, when there is no such thing. Please stop,” he said, according to the Malay-language daily.
His remarks came after Ismail declined to comment on speculation that Jalaluddin, the Pertang assemblyman and Jelebu MP, could replace him as menteri besar.
“As of today, I am still the menteri besar,” Ismail told reporters yesterday, offering no further comment on the claims surrounding his position.
Speculation about a possible leadership challenge surfaced last month when FMT reported, citing an unnamed source, that Negeri Sembilan Umno was considering a no-confidence motion against Ismail.
Jalaluddin denied the claim, while Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said he would prevent any such move.

The latest speculation comes just three months after Ismail was sworn in on August 2, following a state election in which Barisan Nasional (BN) won 18 seats, Pakatan Harapan 11 and Perikatan Nasional (PN) seven.
Jalaluddin also rejected suggestions that separate camps had emerged within Negeri Sembilan Umno, including factions allegedly aligned with him and Ismail.
He said assemblymen should put aside perceptions of internal divisions and focus on their responsibilities to voters.
He urged state leaders to support one another rather than engage in disputes that could distract from the administration’s work.
Addressing questions about his audience with the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, Jalaluddin said the meeting had taken place at the ruler’s request.
He said he would comply whenever summoned by the ruler, both as a party leader and as a subject.
Jalaluddin expressed hope that the state’s political tensions could be resolved soon if all parties worked towards unity.

d2213a0009d6652d: PETALING JAYA: Muhyiddin Yassin mencadangkan Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim memecat menteri tidak sehaluan sambil mendakwa mereka akan menggagalkan segala dasar kerajaan.
Bekas perdana menteri itu, berkata ia patut dipertimbang memandangkan perbalahan terbuka antara pemimpin Barisan Nasional (BN) dengan Anwar, yang boleh menjejaskan kelancaran pelaksanaan dasar.

"Kalau saya jadi perdana menteri, saya dah pecat mereka. Saya rombak Kabinet dan tentukan supaya mereka yang tidak sehaluan dengan saya ini tidak boleh duduk di situ, malah tidak boleh bersama dalam kerajaan.

"Sebab mereka akan menggagalkan segala dasar kerajaan. Mungkin tujuan itulah yang mereka lakukan supaya kerajaan yang dipimpin Anwar akan tumbang," katanya menurut Sinar Harian ketika membantu kempen calon Bersatu di Pengkalan Batu.

Presiden Bersatu berkenaan berkata, pendirian BN semakin menimbulkan kekeliruan memandangkan parti itu masih mempunyai wakil dalam kerajaan termasuk timbalan perdana menteri, menteri, dan timbalan menteri.

Katanya, sebagai anggota kerajaan, sebarang ketidakpuasan hati terhadap dasar atau keputusan pentadbiran sepatutnya diselesaikan menerusi perbincangan di peringkat parti atau Kabinet, bukannya diluahkan secara terbuka.
"Prinsipnya, kalau kita menjadi anggota dalam sebuah kerajaan, kita tidak mengecam kerajaan sendiri atau parti yang ada dalam kerajaan. Itu prinsip biasa.

b95a082a60ce918c: KANGAR: Universiti Islam Antarabangsa Tuanku Syed Sirajuddin (UniSIRAJ) graduates must be trustworthy and uphold integrity, respect differences and stand by the truth - qualities that should guide them as they embark on their careers and future lives.

20e81ad355204cd8: WELLINGTON: New Zealand began counting the votes Saturday in one of the closest elections in its history, with none of the parties expected to secure a majority of seats after a campaign dominated by worries over rising costs of living and the economy.
Kiwis are struggling to make ends meet – the price of basic goods remains stubbornly high, and unemployment is at its highest in more than a decade.
The war in the Middle East and the subsequent global fuel shock have been widely blamed for the hit to New Zealand's trade-dependent economy.

Prime Minister Christopher Luxon is hoping his right-wing coalition can cling to power with promises of no new taxes after three fractious years in office, two failed bids by his own National Party to oust him as leader and an economy in the doldrums.
He has told AFP he sees himself as a "super salesman" for the country and vowed to sign more free trade deals if re-elected.
Former premier Chris Hipkins' centre-left Labour have promised help with living costs, from free doctor's visits and prescriptions to a cap on public transport fares.
He said Friday he was sure his party would "exceed expectations".

But neither is expected to win enough seats in New Zealand's parliament to govern alone, focusing intense attention on the country's minor parties, in particular the upstart centrist Opportunity Party.
Under the country's mixed-member proportional representation (MMP) system, voters must tick two options - a general party list as well as an individual member to represent their electorate.
Opinion polls in the lead-up to the vote put Opportunity over 5% – the threshold needed to gain seats in parliament without an electorate candidate win.
Anti-establishment feeling
The party is led by former KPMG consultant Qiulae Wong, who has vowed kinder, gentler politics and said she could work with either of the two parties if elected.
"I think New Zealanders are really tired of politicians' name-calling, the bickering, and the political point-scoring," she told AFP last week.
"They want something different, and they really want some hope and optimism for the future."
David Capie, a professor at Victoria University of Wellington, said voter fatigue with the two establishment parties was fuelling Wong's rise.
"In some ways, it looks to me a bit like a bit of a blank slate where people are projecting what they would like," he said.
"I don't think many New Zealanders have actually gone and read the details of Opportunity's manifesto, but it's got a very telegenic, very reasonable leader."
A final opinion poll released on Friday put Labour at 30% of the vote, just ahead of the National Party.
At a Labour event in Upper Hutt near Wellington on Saturday, party workers were quietly confident they had secured the largest number of seats.
Prime Minister Luxon has said he's "given up on polls" and urged voters on Friday to "stick to the plan that's working".
"Don't risk a Labour government."
Prices 'too high'
The centre-left party was turfed out of office in 2023, having struggled to inspire voters following the resignation of former prime minister Jacinda Ardern, who became a global progressive icon.
Her replacement, Hipkins, hasn't quite inherited her star quality – instead portraying himself as an everyman, joking about his poor dress sense, love of sausage rolls and passion for DIY.
The party will also likely need to govern in coalition with the left-wing Green Party, which has surged to record support with a focus on the rising costs of living.
On the streets of Wellington, New Zealanders told AFP they were struggling to get by and thinking twice about paying for things they had once taken for granted.
"The prices are really high," said Jay Ikaua, a cultural advisor.
"I have to make conscious decisions. Do I buy that? Do I not buy that?"
"And it's the things we need – public transport, food."
e5578984dc190125: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — China Communications Construction (ECRL) Sdn Bhd (CCCECRL) has completed and handed over Phase 1 of the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) project to project owner Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL), marking a key milestone ahead of the railway’s scheduled commercial launch on December 12.
The 523km Phase 1 alignment stretches from Kota Bharu in Kelantan to Gombak in Selangor and comprises 16 stations, including passenger stations and combined passenger-freight terminals.

MRL chief executive officer Datuk Seri Darwis Abdul Razak said the completion of the Kota Bharu-Gombak rail network would strengthen connectivity between the east and west coasts of Peninsular Malaysia.
“Backed by a modern and state-of-the-art railway system, ECRL’s commercial operations will serve as a catalyst for economic growth and sustainable development.
“We anticipate the ECRL to spur investment opportunities, drive tourism growth, foster job creation, and develop new logistics hubs and industrial parks in the East Coast states,” said Darwis.
According to CCCECRL, the Phase 1 network includes 41 tunnels and 218 viaducts spanning a combined 154km. Among its key engineering features is the 16.39km twin-bore Genting Tunnel.
CCCECRL managing director Deng Bo said the handover represented a major step towards establishing a fully integrated rail link across Peninsular Malaysia.
“The delivery of a fully operational railway system for ECRL Phase 1 represents a defining milestone for cross-peninsular connectivity,” he said.
CCCECRL said its focus has now shifted to Phase 2, which will extend the rail line from Gombak to Port Klang.

Upon completion of the full 665km corridor, the ECRL is expected to provide a direct landbridge linking Kuantan Port and Port Klang, while supporting logistics, industrial development and freight transport across Peninsular Malaysia.
3ab5ca169a14f061: CHUKAI, Nov 7 — The Malaysian Agricultural Research and Development Institute (Mardi) will tighten its safety standard operating procedures (SOPs) and improve safety management for field staff following the death of one of its employees after being stung by bees at the Mardi Kemaman Station in Ayer Putih, near here, last month.

“Mardi management takes staff safety seriously, especially for those working in the field. We have discussed this matter at the meeting, and follow-up measures will be implemented to tighten the SOPs and ensure that all work instructions are complied with.

“Meetings on occupational safety and health will also be held regularly to ensure that safety aspects are continuously monitored and improvements can be made from time to time,” she said in a statement today.
