b2aa66cff7a133e2: MELAKA, Nov 7 — The government has not issued any directive for the public to stock up on food supplies for a 72-hour period as recommended by the Federation of Malaysian Consumer Associations (Fomca).
Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu advised consumers not to panic buy, but instead to continue shopping according to their daily needs as usual.

“We do acknowledge that we are concerned about the current situation, including cyber threats, but we have not yet reached the stage of issuing directives for the public to stockpile food supplies,” he said at a press conference after officiating the ‘Himpunan Semarak Tani Jualan Agro Madani’ in Bukit Katil here today.

Yesterday, Fomca advised consumers to stock up on food and basic necessities for a period of at least 72 hours, as a precautionary measure against potential supply disruptions due to global geopolitical uncertainties and natural disasters.
Commenting further, Mohamad assured that the national rice stock is currently sufficient for a period of six months and will continue to be increased.
“The supply of frozen fish is also guaranteed to be sufficient for the next eight months. So, there is no need for excessive purchases.
“Buying goods in excessive quantities will only create problems and make it difficult for other consumers to obtain supplies,” he said.

Mohamad said that the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security (KPKM) is also constantly assessing the current situation, including through collaboration with universities and researchers such as climate change experts.

As an initial preparatory step, he said the Malaysian Fisheries Development Authority (LKIM), along with private traders who have freezing facilities, have been asked to stock up especially on the people’s choice of fish in high demand in the market.
In another development, he said the government aims to implement 5,000 Agro Madani Sales programmes nationwide, compared to the 3,400 programmes that have been held so far.
Mohamad said this programme that allows consumers to buy goods at 10 to 30 per cent cheaper prices aims to ease the people’s cost of living burden, especially in rural and small town areas.

“We cannot hold programmes like these every day because local grocery stores also need to do business. So, we are holding it weekly to give people a chance to save money while also ensuring the sustainability of local traders,” he added.

Meanwhile, KPKM in a statement said that the Himpunan Semarak Tani @ Jualan Agro Madani (JAM) Mega Negeri Melaka 2026, which is taking place over three days from yesterday, aims to attract 20,000 visitors and benefit 30,000 households.
The ministry set the sales value at RM500,000, involving 109 sales and exhibition lots that brings together 83 entrepreneurs and exhibitors from departments and agencies.

Today’s programme also witnessed the handover of incentives amounting to RM437,450 to five entrepreneurs through the Agropreneur NextGen Start-Up Grant, the High Impact Product (HIP) Matching Grant, and the Market Development and Matching Incentive for Micro Products of the Agricultural-Based Industry (IAT) for Melaka State Entrepreneurs 2026.
“This initiative reflects KPKM’s commitment to empowering local agri-food entrepreneurs and supporting the development of high-impact products,” according to the statement.

KPKM announced that as of October 2026, the Melaka branch of the Federal Agricultural Marketing Authority (FAMA) has implemented 258 JAM programmes involving 3,300 entrepreneurs with a total sales value of RM5.87 million.
Overall, a total of 3,400 JAM programmes have been conducted nationwide from January to November 2026, with sales value exceeding RM80 million and savings for consumers amounting to RM26 million.
“This implementation also involves the participation of 55,000 entrepreneurs and the attendance of over 4.7 million visitors nationwide,” he added. — Bernama
ac99e9cb319c88ac: JOHOR BARU: The special financial assistance of RM1,000 for school bus drivers, announced in the 2027 Budget, is considered timely particularly in helping them navigate cash flow challenges when the school term ends.

Malaysian School Bus Operators and Drivers Association president Dr M. Muruga said the aid is highly significant, given that school bus fare collections typically take a temporary hit during school holidays.

Dr. Muruga, who also serves as the chairman of the Johor State School Bus Operators and Drivers Association, added that the assistance serves as a meaningful recognition for school bus drivers, who have long hoped for specific attention and support from the government.

"This is a form of recognition from the government, and we are very proud that, after such a long time, the welfare of school bus drivers has finally received attention through the 2027 Budget," he said when contacted by Bernama.
He said the coalition has over 3,000 registered school bus driver members nationwide, 60 per cent of whom are women.
He urged drivers who have not yet registered to join the association in their respective states, ensuring they do not miss out on any information or assistance initiatives.

Meanwhile, Mohd Suhaimi Saidi, chairman of a coalition representing three Johor Baru–Singapore cross-border taxi associations, noted that the assistance would help ease the financial burden on taxi drivers, especially amidst a challenging economic climate and rising costs of living.
He said the grant is also highly significant for taxi drivers, helping them cover vehicle maintenance costs as well as daily living expenses.
"This is a godsend for us, as taxi drivers are also facing threats from e-hailing services.
"This assistance goes a long way in easing their burden, especially since it is being provided just ahead of the Deepavali festival," he said, noting that the association has a total of 189 members.

The government is distributing a one-off special financial aid of RM1,000 to 38,000 taxi drivers, including those operating rental cars, as well as 15,000 school bus drivers nationwide, funded by proceeds from the sale of special 'H' series vehicle registration numbers.
While tabling the 2027 Budget, Anwar said this aid is being provided as part of an effort to return such revenue to the people.
d410f93a37aaeba2: JASIN: Umno and PAS’s youth wings will lodge police reports nationwide against Attorney-General Dusuki Mokhtar over a suggestion to defer Najib Razak’s house arrest pending a review of the conditional pardon and the High Court’s Order of Discharge.
Umno Youth chief Dr Akmal Saleh said the move was necessary to allow an investigation into allegations that Dusuki had abused his powers.

“That is why we believe this matter cannot be allowed to go unchallenged. I have discussed this with my (PAS) counterpart, and we will mobilise party members nationwide to lodge police reports against the AG,” he said after attending a campaign programme in the Merlimau state constituency.

Earlier today, Istana Negara said any action challenging the conditional pardon order allowing Najib to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest would amount to defying the Yang di-Pertuan Agong's authority.
Akmal also questioned how long the AG had taken to seek legal clarification on the order for Najib’s conditional pardon, which he said was issued on Sept 18.
“How much more time does he need to obtain such clarification? This is what we want investigated. If there has been an abuse of power, we cannot simply let it go,” he said.
Akmal said Najib was entitled to serve his sentence under house arrest following the full payment of the RM50 million fine.
He said that although Najib had committed an offence and served his sentence, the rights accorded to him under the royal pardon must be respected.
In a separate statement, Umno called for stern action against those who defied the conditional pardon order granted to Najib.

“Malaysia cannot be allowed to be governed and administered by those who clearly disregard the provisions enshrined in the Federal Constitution,” it said, referring to the king’s royal prerogative to grant pardons.
Yesterday, Umno announced that it had settled the RM50 million fine imposed on its former president after raising funds through a donation drive.
The Kuala Lumpur High Court subsequently issued an Order for Discharge after the payment was recorded.

However, the Attorney-General's Chambers said the implementation of the house arrest order should be deferred temporarily to allow it to examine legal questions relating to the pardon order and the implications of the court order.
7e2dd95045c32706: KUCHING, Nov 7 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Amar Fadillah Yusof has brushed off speculation that he may contest in the 13th Sarawak state election.
Asked by reporters whether there was any truth to speculation that he could be among the candidates in the upcoming polls, Fadillah said he was unaware of it.
“That is speculation, so there is no need to comment. I myself do not know,” he said.

Fadillah, who is also Petra Jaya MP and minister of energy transition and water transformation, was speaking to reporters after officiating the Royal Malaysia Police Sarawak Contingent futsal court at the Sarawak Contingent Police headquarters here on Saturday.
He was also asked about the key dates announced by the Election Commission (EC) for the state election.

Fadillah, who is Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB) senior vice president and Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) parliamentary chief whip, said PBB and GPS election machinery was already prepared, with preparations having been carried out since the previous state election.
“Actually, our work is carried out all the time. Since the last election, we have already started working. This is just the democratic process where we have to hold an election,” he said.
He said PBB’s election machinery was ready to assist all GPS component parties, with logistics and other arrangements already in place ahead of nomination day.
“All the groundwork has been arranged, including logistics and everything. We are ready and waiting for nomination day, after which the machinery will start going to the ground,” he said.
On the 14-day campaign period, the longest in Sarawak’s electoral history, Fadillah said GPS respected the EC’s decision and would prepare accordingly.
“That is the discretion or jurisdiction of the EC. As a party, we respect whatever decision is made.
“For us, we need to prepare ourselves. If it is 14 days, we prepare for 14 days. If it is 10 days, then we work for 10 days. That is the authority of the EC,” he said.
He said the election was ultimately about giving voters the opportunity to decide who would administer Sarawak for the next five years.
“The election is only for us to hand it back to the people to determine who will administer our state, particularly for the next five years,” he said. — The Borneo Post
55da2e602eb0476f: KUALA LUMPUR: DAP has yet to discuss who it would nominate to replace Anthony Loke as transport minister once his resignation takes effect.

bee8f6f7b739d24d: SINGAPORE, Nov 7 — Heading across the Causeway for the Deepavali long weekend?

7c46cd2cfc11884d: GEORGE TOWN: Diversity remains Penang's cornerstone of unity, turning societal differences into shared economic and educational progress for all communities, said Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow.

In his Deepavali message, Chow said that beyond commemorating the symbolic triumph of light over darkness and good over evil, the festival served as a timely reminder of the need to build a prosperous, harmonious and mutually respectful society.
"In Penang, our diversity of race, religion, language and culture is the very strength that unites us.

"Differences are not a reason to drift apart but an opportunity to complement one another and build a shared future through education, economic development and well-being accessible to every segment of society," he said.

Underscoring education as an indispensable pillar for the younger generation, Chow highlighted the state government's ongoing investments to strengthen Tamil vernacular education, digital competency and exposure to Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM).
In April this year, the Penang government channelled RM2.42 million towards educational development in Tamil schools across the state.
Of this amount, RM1.34 million was allocated through the Penang Education Council (PEC) to upgrade digital infrastructure and STEM capabilities.

A further RM768,901 was disbursed to 28 SJKT through their Parent-Teacher Associations (PTAs) for routine maintenance and facility upgrades, while RM194,400 went to 11 kindergartens located within SJKTs to support early childhood education.

Chow said academic advancement must be complemented by grassroots cultural preservation, praising community-led programmes such as the free Tamil classes organised by the Lebuh Pasar Village Community Management Council.
Addressing structural concerns, Chow reaffirmed the state's commitment to helping all 28 SJKTs in Penang secure permanent land titles.
As of June 2026, land plots had been secured for five schools, with five more targeted over the next two to three years.
The state has also provided a 2.368-acre site to facilitate the relocation of SJKT Rajaji in Air Itam.
Looking ahead under the 2027 Madani Budget framework, Chow said Penang would deepen cooperation with federal agencies, civil society and the private sector to widen socio-economic opportunities.

917fbbb9fb038d15: PETALING JAYA: Jabatan Peguam Negara (AGC) menjelaskan permohonan menangguhkan pelaksanaan tahanan dalam rumah Najib Razak bukan percubaan mempertikaikan pengampunan bersyarat diberikan kepada bekas perdana menteri itu.
Sebaliknya, isu dipersoalkan adalah kesan undang-undang bagi perintah pelepasan dikeluarkan Mahkamah Tinggi Kuala Lumpur semalam, susulan pembayaran denda RM50 juta oleh Najib.
"AGC menegaskan bahawa ia tidak sama sekali mempertikai, mengenepi atau berhasrat untuk menggantung perintah pengampunan bersyarat diperkenankan Seri Paduka Baginda Yang di-Pertuan Agong.

"AGC sentiasa menjunjung kedaulatan undang-undang, menghormati kedudukan institusi Yang di-Pertuan Agong serta mengiktiraf prerogatif pengampunan baginda sebagaimana diperuntukkan di bawah Perkara 42 Perlembagaan Persekutuan," katanya dalam kenyataan.
AGC turut menjelaskan isu dibangkitkan tidak menyentuh tentang keesahan atau kewibawaan perintah pengampunan bersyarat tersebut.

Pihaknya menekankan perintah pelepasan daripada Mahkamah Tinggi Kuala Lumpur kepada Jabatan Penjara, yang menyatakan: "Dan bahawasanya denda tersebut yang berjumlah RM50 juta kini telah dibayar kepada mahkamah ini: Ini adalah untuk memberi kuasa kepada anda untuk melepaskan Najib Razak tersebut […] serta-merta."
Perintah mahkamah yang sama juga menyatakan Najib perlu menjalani baki hukumannya bawah tahanan dalam rumah sehingga 23 Ogos 2028.

"Justeru, timbul persoalan undang-undang mengenai skop dan kesan arahan pelepasan tersebut, khususnya sama ada pelepasan yang diperintahkan hanya berkaitan dengan pembayaran denda atau membolehkan baki hukuman penjara SRC International diteruskan melalui tahanan rumah, atau sama ada perintah tersebut membawa kesan hukuman dalam kes SRC International telah selesai."

Katanya, ia mempunyai kaitan langsung dengan perintah Mahkamah Tinggi dalam kes 1MDB yang menetapkan hukuman penjara dalam kes terbabit hendaklah bermula selepas hukuman dalam kes SRC International selesai dijalani.
Mahkamah Tinggi telah memerintahkan Najib menjalani hukuman penjara 15 tahun bagi pertuduhan salah guna kuasa dan pengubahan wang haram selepas hukuman kes SRC International beliau tamat.
AGC menyatakan, jika hukuman kes SRC International masih berkuat kuasa, baki tempoh hukuman tersebut hendaklah dijalani mengikut perintah pengampunan bersyarat berkenaan.
"Sekiranya hukuman dalam kes SRC International masih berkuat-kuasa, maka tidak timbul persoalan mengenai pelaksanaan baki hukuman tersebut selaras dengan perintah pengampunan bersyarat.
"Sebaliknya, sekiranya hukuman SRC International telah selesai dari segi undang-undang, maka perlu ditentukan kesannya terhadap permulaan hukuman dalam kes 1MDB.
"Kedua-dua kemungkinan ini mempunyai implikasi undang-undang yang berbeza dan tidak sewajarnya diputuskan berdasarkan andaian atau tafsiran sebelah pihak," katanya.
AGC berkata, implikasi undang-undang perintah mahkamah tersebut hendaklah dirujuk kepada mahkamah dengan segera bagi mendapatkan penentuan dan arahan yang jelas.

"Adalah tidak tepat untuk menyamakan pendirian AGC bahawa sesuatu persoalan undang-undang memerlukan penentuan mahkamah dengan dakwaan peguam negara mengambil alih prerogatif pengampunan Seri Paduka Baginda," katanya mengulas kenyataan pasukan peguam Najib, Shafee & Co, yang mendakwa peguam negara bertindak melampaui kuasanya, mengingkari titah diraja, dan meneruskan penahanan Najib secara tidak sah.

Terdahulu, Istana Negara hari ini menyatakan Yang di-Pertuan Agong menegaskan perintah pengampunan bersyarat tersebut adalah jelas, nyata, dan tanpa sebarang ambiguiti, serta tidak mempunyai kaitan dengan mana-mana kes lain yang melibatkan bekas perdana menteri itu.
461b468813ff4469: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 7 — The Ministry of Energy Transition and Water Transformation (Petra) is enhancing its preparedness for the 2026/2027 North-east Monsoon season, focusing on early planning, resource coordination and operational readiness.

In a statement today, Petra said preparations for the Northeast Monsoon, which began on October 27 and is expected to last until March 2027, are being coordinated through the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID) to ensure effective and comprehensive flood risk management.

The ministry said the DID National Flood Forecasting and Warning Centre (PRABN) issued 103 bulletins, comprising 64 early flood forecast bulletins and 39 flood warning bulletins, during the 2025/2026 North-east Monsoon season from November 13, 2025, to March 31, 2026.

“Some 14.8 million short message service (SMS) alerts were sent to residents in high-risk areas, according to records from the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC),” the statement said.
“A total of 799 flood incidents were recorded nationwide, comprising 480 monsoon floods, 274 flash floods, 25 cases of stagnant flooding and 20 coastal floods,” it said.

Petra said the flooding was attributed to several factors, including river overflows, internal drainage problems and high tides, as well as localised issues such as blocked drains, uncontrolled development, land clearing and improper waste disposal.

In preparation for the 2026/2027 North-east Monsoon, the DID was carrying out round-the-clock monitoring throughout the year using flood forecasting models covering 36 river basins, supported by 2,237 telemetry-based hydrological stations that record rainfall and river water levels, the ministry said.
The ministry said 614 flood warning sirens and 197 surveillance cameras were also in place at strategic locations nationwide to support flood monitoring and early warning efforts.

Petra said 3,045 locations nationwide had been identified as flood hotspots, having experienced flooding at least three times in the past three years, with Kelantan recording the highest number at 609, followed by Pahang (572) and Terengganu (460).
In terms of operational readiness, the ministry said 1,079 water control gates and 285 pump houses nationwide are in good condition and ready to support flood control operations.
Petra said 580 portable emergency pumps of various capacities were also ready for deployment to critical areas to mitigate flood risks.
Meanwhile, the ministry said 16 DID control dams and 781 flood retention ponds were being monitored, while maintenance work continued in high-risk river basins.
“Cooperation with MCMC and telecommunications companies is ongoing to facilitate the dissemination of flood warnings via SMS to residents in high-risk areas,” it said.

Petra said it was also working with state authorities to establish standard operating procedures (SOPs) for dam water releases to enhance floodwater retention capacity during the Northeast Monsoon season.

To mitigate flood risks, the ministry said 1,638 minor projects were implemented in 2026 at a cost of RM652 million, while 342 development projects under the First Rolling Plan of the 13th Malaysia Plan were approved for implementation this year, with an allocation of RM3.2 billion.

Petra also advised the public to stay informed of official flood forecasts and warnings issued by the DID through the Public InfoBanjir website and MyPublicInfoBanjir mobile application, which is available for download from the Google Play Store and Apple App Store. — Bernama
976b2cb57b82d2b9: PUTRAJAYA: The Immigration Department has collected RM91.78 million in compounds involving 32,052 people for offences under immigration laws from Jan 1 to Oct 31 this year.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said of the total, RM50.04 million involved 2,459 employers, while the remaining RM41.74 million involved 29,593 undocumented migrants.

He said the figures showed that immigration enforcement was not solely focused on undocumented migrants, but also involved action against employers who violated regulations governing the employment of foreign workers.
"This means that 54.5 per cent of the total compound amount collected involved employers.

"This figure is important because immigration enforcement should not be viewed solely through action against undocumented migrants, but also through action against those who violate regulations governing the employment of foreign workers," he said in a Facebook post today.

He said the presence of foreigners staying or working in the country without valid documents remained a concern, not only in terms of compliance with immigration laws but also the management of foreigners, as well as public safety and order.

He said such concerns deserved attention, but the public also needed to understand that efforts to address the issue involved various forms of enforcement action, including action against employers who committed immigration offences.
He said addressing the issue of undocumented migrants required public cooperation, including providing the authorities with information on activities suspected of violating immigration regulations.
He said public cooperation must operate within a clear legal framework, while enforcement action could only be carried out by agencies empowered to do so under the law.
dffa28280c0ebf1f: KUALA MUDA: Differences in race and religion have done little to weaken the bond between Nur Najihah Muhaimin, 35, and T Avieenya, 33, whose friendship has lasted 13 years.
Despite living far apart, Nur Najihah, affectionately known as Jea, and Avieenya, or Vinya, remain close and consider each other family.
A TikTok video showed Jea, who lives in Gurun, Kedah, picking up her three-month-old son, Umar, from Vinya's home in Teluk Intan, Perak, after her friend had looked after him.

Jea, who works for a corporate company, said she had recently spent time with Vinya, who offered to look after her three-month-old son, Umar Alejandro Ahmad Qusairi, with help from her mother so that Jea could rest.
"I was visiting my family in Teluk Intan at the time, so I met up with Vinya.
"After we went out, Vinya told me to go home and get some rest. She said she and her mother could help look after Umar.
"Vinya did not ask for any payment. She simply wanted to help. I shared the video on TikTok as a keepsake.
"I never expected it to attract so much attention, with most people leaving positive comments," she said.
Jea said their friendship began when they worked at neighbouring premises in Bandar Baru Teluk Intan.
At the time, Jea was working as a coordinator at the Ummah Education Centre, while Vinya's father owned a photography shop next door.
Their friendship grew naturally, and Jea said she now regarded Vinya as part of her family.

She said Vinya had also joined her in various community initiatives organised through non-governmental organisations, including Buku Jalanan Teluk Intan, Sukarelawan Aspirasi Teluk Intan and Wanita Muda Amanah Perak.
"I used to live in Teluk Intan, and whenever there was a programme, Vinya would join me if she was free.
"She was also actively involved in Buku Jalanan Teluk Intan and our Ramadan picnics, which have been organised since 2013.
"We have shared so many memories. Among the activities we took part in was distributing flowers during the Maal Hijrah celebrations."
Jea described Vinya as one in a million and said she deeply valued their friendship.
"It is not just Vinya. I have also grown close to her family, especially her parents.
"Her mother has invited me to their home for Deepavali, and Vinya has even bought me a sari to wear for the celebration.
"I hope our friendship lasts for many more years, that we will always be there for each other during difficult times and continue creating wonderful memories together," she said.

1ab9d39bccd8d054: KUALA LUMPUR: Johor Darul Ta'zim are closing in on a fifth consecutive FA Cup final appearance, with the prospect of playing for the trophy on home turf adding further incentive as the semi-final second legs take place on Sunday.

The defending champions hold a 2-0 aggregate lead over Brunei DPMM ahead of their return leg at the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium, while Selangor travel to Kuching with a narrower 2-1 advantage over Kuching City.

JDT took control of their tie in the first leg in Bandar Seri Begawan through goals from Bergson da Silva and Eddy Israfilov, but head coach Xisco Munoz has warned his players against taking their advantage for granted.
"It is never enough when you are with JDT," said Munoz.
"A two-goal lead is a positive start, but it is not enough to satisfy us. We will enter the second leg on the front foot, attacking to score more goals in front of our home supporters."
Meanwhile, DPMM head coach Jamie McAllister believes his side can still turn the tie around, with an early goal potentially changing the contest.
"I believe we can do it. It is indeed a tough challenge, but we must go there with the belief that we can turn it around," he said.
"I think the first goal will be very important. If we manage to score the first goal, our chances of getting right back into this contest become much better."

The stakes are particularly high for JDT after the Malaysian Football League confirmed that the FA Cup final will be held at the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium due to ongoing upgrading works at the National Stadium in Bukit Jalil.
A victory over DPMM would put the Southern Tigers within reach of lifting the trophy in front of their own supporters.
In the other semi-final, Selangor face a difficult trip to Petra Jaya to take on a Kuching City side buoyed by a historic continental victory.

The Cats stunned South Korean side Gangwon 2-0 in the Asian Champions League Two (ACL2) in midweek, but head coach Aidil Sharin Sahak has urged his players to quickly turn their attention back to domestic matters.
"Even though we achieved a great victory, we cannot afford to be comfortable or complacent," said Aidil.
"Instead, we must refocus and make preparations for this Sunday's match. Our journey is still long with many more battles ahead."
Kuching's preparations have also been complicated by injuries to two key players.
Brazilian defender Gabriel Peres is expected to be sidelined for two months after undergoing knee surgery, while striker Ronald Ngah Wanja is also out through injury.
"Many might not understand how difficult the situation is when a team loses key pillars, especially when having to navigate multiple crucial competitions," Aidil said.
Selangor, who won the first leg 2-1 at the MBPJ Stadium, will be looking to protect their advantage and book a place in the final.
However, coach Kim Pan Gon knows his side will face a difficult atmosphere in Borneo and has called on his players to show the determination needed to get through.
"We know it is going to be a very difficult match, but we have the spirit and the desire to reach the final," Pan Gon said.

"The players have great fighting spirit, and for me, that spirit and hunger are vital. We know the harsh circumstances we will have to face, but we will become stronger and stronger. We want to be in the final."

1da594ba90393a2a: MELAKA, Nov 7 — The first week of campaigning for the 16th Melaka State Election has been relatively subdued, with parties focusing mainly on house-to-house visits and manifesto promises to win over voters.

Pakatan Harapan (PH) has offered an alternative to Barisan Nasional (BN) through its “Aspirasi Melaka Rumah Kita” manifesto, which outlines three main pillars and 12 priorities, including a clean, transparent and efficient administration, the Smart Melaka transformation, expanding economic opportunities for youths and strengthening the tourism industry.

Apart from highlighting solutions to issues such as the cost of living, employment opportunities, housing and public welfare, PH is also wooing young voters by offering to allocate 30 per cent of local authority work contracts to young men and women, while fielding several young candidates to appeal to this voter segment.

The campaign machinery of PH’s component parties has also been strengthened through better coordination, including the establishment of a PH Main Operations Room, and the participation of the top leadership of PKR, DAP and Amanah in grassroots engagement programmes.

Commenting on PH’s campaign efforts so far, Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) Negeri Sembilan Branch Faculty of Administrative Science and Policy Studies senior lecturer Mujibu Abd Muis said the coalition still had room to differentiate its manifesto from BN’s, despite both coalitions being part of the federal Unity Government.

He said the differences needed to be translated into policy approaches and priorities, with PH seeking to highlight the Smart Melaka transformation agenda, economic opportunities for youths, more transparent governance and tourism sector reforms suited to the state’s context.

“However, their positions in the federal government could still create a political dilemma for both PH and BN. As such, neither coalition can rely too heavily on criticisms towards the government, as both share responsibility for national administration.
“PH needs to prove that it offers added value in terms of state administration, rather than merely bringing a different political brand,” he told Bernama.

Mujibu said PH had also succeeded in highlighting several issues closely affecting people’s daily lives, particularly traffic congestion, employment opportunities, housing and infrastructure. However, the welfare of fishermen and problems involving local amenities require more specific attention.
Issues such as coastal erosion, jetty facilities, fishermen’s operating costs, water supply disruptions and road problems require localised and practical solutions.

On the candidacy of young candidates, Mujibu said the move had the potential to inject new life into PH’s campaign through an image of renewal, political energy and the ability to connect with younger generations. However, age alone does not guarantee voter acceptance.

“What matters more is credibility, the ability to understand issues concerning employment, wages, housing and the cost of living, as well as the candidates’ ability to represent young people’s voices in the decision-making process.
“In electoral politics, young voters do not necessarily choose young candidates, as they prefer candidates who understand their problems and can offer solutions,” he said.

On cooperation among PKR, DAP and Amanah, Mujibu said seat allocations and agreements at the leadership level did not necessarily guarantee an automatic transfer of votes at the grassroots level. Therefore, PH needed to ensure that supporters of all three parties accepted the candidates fielded, avoid internal competition and ensure that their campaign machinery delivered consistent messages, he said.
“PH is contesting 24 of the 28 state seats. Therefore, it must not only defend the five seats it won in the 2021 state election but also prove its ability to make inroads into new areas.
“The target of winning 18 seats announced by PH’s leadership is an ambitious one and requires genuinely effective cross-party support,” he said.

Mujibu said PH’s biggest challenge was to convince voters that the coalition had the capability and plans to govern Melaka, including in terms of leadership, coalition stability, development priorities and fiscal discipline.
He said PH needed to focus on practical solutions to issues involving employment, traffic congestion, housing, welfare and infrastructure.

Meanwhile, UiTM Melaka Branch Faculty of Communication and Media Studies senior lecturer Dr Shafezah Abdul Wahab said PH had managed to establish itself selectively as an alternative to BN, particularly in urban areas, but might still face challenges in securing grassroots support.
On PH’s manifesto offers, she said issues involving the cost of living, employment opportunities, affordable housing and digital transformation should be key campaign priorities.

However, she said their effectiveness would depend on how realistic the proposals were and whether they were backed by clear implementation mechanisms rather than being merely election promises. — Bernama
1e5fbd84dabc758a: PONTIAN: Several Umno leaders have lodged a police report over the delay in implementing house arrest for former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak.
Pontian Umno leaders, led by division chief Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Maslan, lodged the report at the Benut police station.
This came after Umno demanded the immediate implementation of Najib's house arrest and action against anyone who defied His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia's order on the matter.

Najib's lawyers have also demanded that he be immediately transferred from Kajang Prison to serve the remainder of his jail sentence under house arrest following Istana Negara's clarification that all conditions of his conditional royal pardon have been fulfilled.
Muhammad Farhan Muhammad Shafee, a member of Najib's legal team, said there was no longer any basis for the authorities to keep Najib at Kajang Prison.
The Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) today said seeking a court ruling on Najib's house arrest did not override the King's power to grant pardons.
It said the King's constitutional authority to grant pardons and the courts' power to interpret the legal effect of an order were separate matters.
685a9bbb649eb344: KUALA LUMPUR: The Selangor irrigation and drainage department has installed additional pumps and upgraded existing ones at Jalan Resak and Desa Subang Perantau in Kampung Melayu Subang, the worst flood-hit areas in the Klang Valley recently.

The department said the existing pump at Jalan Resak had been replaced with a new, higher-capacity unit, while the original pump had been relocated to Desa Subang Perantau, giving the latter area two pumps to help discharge water into Sungai Pelempas, Berita Harian reported.
"An assessment following the floods on Nov 2 and Nov 4, when rainfall exceeded 100mm, found that a higher-capacity pump was needed at Jalan Resak.

"This is mainly because internal drainage flows into a pond at Jalan Resak before being channelled into Sungai Pelempas. As such, we replaced the pump at Jalan Resak with a new unit with a capacity of 280 litres per second (l/s).

"Desa Subang Perantau (Jalan Ikhlas), which is located downstream, requires more high-capacity pumps due to the higher risk of backwater overflow from the Kampung Baru Subang Bridge in the area," the department said in a statement.
The move is a short-term mitigation measure to drain internal runoff and river overflow, should it occur, pending the implementation of the Sungai Pelempas project.
The project entails the raising of low-lying sections of the Sungai Pelempas riverbank or bund by 0.5m to 1m to prevent overflow during heavy rainfall.
The department attributed the slow receding of floodwaters in both areas to heavy rainfall, with Jalan Resak recording 116.5mm on Nov 2 and Desa Subang Perantau receiving 91.5mm on Nov 4.
"The high water level in Sungai Pelempas makes it difficult for water from internal drainage systems to flow into the river. Hence, we have provided pumps to facilitate this process.
"In addition, the affected areas are low-lying, with limited and poorly organised internal drainage systems," the department said.
The department said its planned short-term measures included upgrading the pump capacity at Jalan Resak from 140 l/s to 280 l/s, while providing a 280 l/s pump at Jalan Ikhlas.

It has also installed flap gates at drainage outlets leading into the river from internal drains and ditches within privately owned lots that could potentially allow river water to flow back into the internal drainage system.

"We have also identified locations for the urgent construction of floodwalls in areas affected by overflow from Sungai Pelumut, as well as potential sites for retention ponds and river widening along Sungai Pelempas.
"Through the Sungai Damansara flood mitigation project, the department will also widen and deepen the downstream stretch of Sungai Damansara and remove obstructions from the river," it said.

e5a8fdc79faa7994: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 7 — Penang’s traditional performing arts master Che Mat Jusoh and Teochew iron-rod puppeteer Toh Ai Hwa were among the recipients of the Living National Heritage Award (Wakoh) this year.

Tourism and creative economy state exco Wong Hon Wai said the duo were among a total of 11 personalities from all over the country who were recognised by the Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture (Motac) under the Sixth National Heritage Declaration 2026.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM) traditional performing arts master Che Mat Jusoh, 72, was awarded the 2026 Living National Heritage Figure (Wakoh) recognition. — Picture courtesy of USM

He said there were others from Penang who have received the Wakoh recognition prior to this such as Omar Md Hashim for boria, Mohd Bahroodin Ahmad for boria, ronggeng and Penang baba and nyonya culture and Abu Bakar Jaafar, also for boria.

“These three were the 2023 recipients and this year, we have two recipients and Toh is the first Penang woman to ever receive the Wakoh award,” he said in his speech at the opening of the 2026 International Performing Arts Symposium and Puppetry Spectacular, Moved to Life: Tradition and Reinvention in Asian Puppet Theatre here today.
A total of 69 heritage items, including popular foods, have been declared as National Heritage 2026 and three of Penang’s foods were also listed.
Wong said Penang’s nasi kandar was declared as a national heritage alongside char koay kak and pasembur.

“So these three are the heritage food from Penang which have already been recognised by the Penang state government under the state heritage in January this year, and now, have been elevated to the national heritage status,” he said.
Meanwhile, National Heritage Department director-general Mohamad Muda Bahadin said the Wakoh recognition is not the end point.
“It should instead serve as a catalyst for efforts to pass on knowledge, provide training and involve a new generation,” he said in his speech.

A Teochew iron-rod performance by the Giak Lai Teochew puppet troupe. — Picture by Opalyn Mok

“The survival of Teochew iron-rod puppetry requires more young practitioners, the documentation of knowledge and repertoire, the preservation of traditional music, and continuing opportunities for the art to be performed and learned,” he added.
He said the art form also reflects Malaysia’s rich cultural diversity.
“Although rooted in the traditions of the Teochew community, its development in Penang has made it part of the nation’s history and cultural treasures, which we should all appreciate,” he said.

He commended the Teochew Puppet and Opera House, especially Ling Goh, Toh’s daughter, for continuing her family’s legacy as a fourth-generation practitioner and introducing this art to the public through education, performances and creative collaborations.

“Today’s programme, which brings together traditional and contemporary puppetry practitioners from various countries, also provides an important opportunity for the exchange of knowledge and the continuation of heritage,” he said.
Among the highlights of the opening ceremony of the symposium at Penang Institute was a tribute to honour Toh’s achievement as an iron-rod puppeteer and a living national heritage.

The symposium, organised by the Teochew Puppet and Opera House, brought together traditional master puppeteers and contemporary artists from Malaysia, China, Hong Kong, India, Japan, Taiwan and the United States for a two-day event today and tomorrow.
The symposium, running from 9am to 6pm on both days, features live performances, talks, artist discussions, demonstrations and hands-on workshops.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

‘Buka Panggung’ featured performances by four Malaysian puppetry traditions (from left) Potehi glove puppetry, Teochew iron-rod puppetry, Malay wayang kulit and string puppetry. — Picture by Opalyn Mok

The opening ceremony started with Buka Panggung, a joint performance featuring four Malaysian puppetry traditions, namely Malay wayang kulit, string puppetry, Potehi glove puppetry and Teochew iron-rod puppetry.

Another highlight is the gathering of Teochew puppetry practitioners from Chaozhou in China, Hong Kong and Malaysia, including Chen Peisen, a nationally recognised master and representative inheritor of China’s Chaozhou iron-rod puppetry tradition.
The programme tomorrow will also include contemporary puppetry with artists such as India’s Anurupa Roy, award-winning American puppeteer Hobey Ford, Japan’s Erina Saji and Taiwan’s Cheng Chia-Yin.

Local groups including Iron Gang Puppet Theatre and Plasticity Theatre Troupe will also participate, while workshops will introduce visitors to object storytelling, Japanese Bunraku-style puppet manipulation and rod-puppet techniques.
There will be two nights of free outdoor puppetry performances at Armenian Park, from 8pm to 11pm, on November 7 and 8.

A wayang kulit performance by Azhar Roslan. — Picture by Opalyn Mok

There will be a screening of the documentary Beyond the Branch followed by a traditional Puppet Battle, featuring wayang kulit, string puppetry, Potehi glove puppetry and Teochew iron-rod puppetry, at the park tonight.
The evening concludes at 10.30pm with Journey to the West: Peril at Gossamer Cave, presented by the Kim Giak Low Choon Teochew Puppet Troupe in collaboration with Filamen.
Tomorrow night, there will be an international showcase featuring traditional and contemporary puppeteers from Malaysia and abroad.
Among the performers are Iron Gang Puppet Theatre, Plasticity, Chen Peisen, Anurupa Roy, Erina Saji, Cheng Chia-Yin and Hobey Ford.
The festival will conclude with a special collaboration involving Roy, Ling Goh and puppeteer Low Zhi Kai.
6fb96bb2eddb674d: GEORGE TOWN: Pantai Jerejak assemblyman Fahmi Zainol has questioned PKR's disciplinary consistency, alleging double standards in the party's handling of misconduct claims against elected representatives.
In a social media post, the former Penang executive councillor questioned the status of party action against another assemblyman recently implicated in a police investigation.
"What is the fate of the recent case involving a Keadilan (PKR) assemblyman?" Fahmi asked.
"As a party member, I feel the treatment has been different, all positions stripped and immediately sacked. Now what does PKR secretary-general (Datuk Dr) Fuziah Salleh have to say?
"Justice has ceased to be justice (Keadilan tidak menjadi keadilan)," he wrote on Facebook.
Fahmi maintained that raising internal grievances did not amount to disloyalty to the party.
"Having lived in loyalty for so long, speaking out does not mean betrayal," he added.
Earlier this year, Fahmi was suspended from his PKR party posts and removed as a state executive councillor after being charged in court with voluntarily causing hurt to his wife.
His remarks follow recent reports of a police investigation involving another Penang lawmaker.
He denied being involved in the latest alleged domestic assault involving a Penang assemblyman.
"The latest case involving a Penang assemblyman is not me," he was quoted as saying.
Penang police said last week that they had recorded statements from four people, including a Penang assemblyman and his wife, over an alleged domestic assault involving the couple.

8af0c19a07f533c8: PETALING JAYA: The Attorney-General's Chambers says its request to defer the implementation of Najib Razak's house arrest was not an attempt to dispute the conditional pardon granted to the former prime minister.
Instead, it said, the issue in question was the legal effect of the Order of Discharge issued by the Kuala Lumpur High Court yesterday following the payment of Najib's RM50 million fine.
“The AGC stresses that it does not in any way dispute, set aside or intend to suspend the conditional pardon order granted by His Majesty the Yang di-Pertuan Agong.

“The AGC has always upheld the rule of law, respected the position of the institution of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, and recognised His Majesty’s prerogative of pardon as provided for under Article 42 of the Federal Constitution.

“In this regard, it is inaccurate to equate the AGC's position that a legal question requires determination by the court with allegations that the attorney-general has usurped His Majesty's prerogative of pardon, ” it said in a statement.
The AGC also stressed that the issue it raised does not concern the validity or authority of the order for the conditional pardon.

It highlighted the Kuala Lumpur High Court’s Order of Discharge to the prisons department, which states: “And whereas the said fine amounting to RM50 million has now been paid into this court: This is to authorise you to discharge the said Najib Razak […] forthwith.”
The same court order also states that Najib is to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028.

"The dispute arose on the scope and effect of the discharge order - whether it focused solely on the payment of the fine and allowed him (Najib) to serve the remaining SRC International sentence on house arrest, or if the discharge order meant that his (six-year) sentence had been completed," the AGC said.
It reiterated that the purported completion of Najib's current SRC International jail sentence has a bearing on his 1MDB case sentence.
The High Court had ordered Najib to serve his 15-year sentence for abuse of power and money laundering after his SRC International sentence ended.
The AGC said if the SRC International sentence is still in force, the remaining term should be served in accordance with the conditional pardon order.
“However, if the sentence has been legally completed, the implications for the start of Najib’s prison term in the 1MDB case must be determined.
"These two scenarios have different legal implications and should not be decided based on assumptions or one-sided interpretations.”
The AGC said the legal implications of the court order should be referred to the court immediately to obtain a clear determination and directions.

“This step is not intended to undermine or frustrate the implementation of the conditional pardon, but rather to avoid any conflict in the implementation of valid orders and ensure that no sentence is enforced unlawfully,” it said in response to Najib’s legal team, Shafee & Co, which accused the attorney-general of acting beyond his authority, disobeying royal decrees, and unlawfully continuing Najib's detention.
Istana Negara said today the king emphasised that the conditional pardon order is clear, explicit and unambiguous, and is not related to any other cases involving the former prime minister.
3aac3b36c0a8d3f4: KUALA LUMPUR: Johor Darul Ta'zim (JDT) and head coach Xisco Munoz have been fined a combined US$13,200 (RM58,000) by the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) following their ill-tempered Asian Champions League Elite (ACLE) clash against Buriram United.
The penalties were handed down by the AFC Disciplinary and Ethics Committee at its Nov 5 meeting, taking JDT's total disciplinary fines for the 2026-2027 campaign to US$15,200 (RM66,800).
That figure includes an earlier US$2,000 (RM8,800) fine imposed on midfielder Eddy Israfilov for his straight red card in the same Sept 15 fixture.

JDT received the heaviest portion of the latest sanctions, with a US$9,450 (RM41,500) fine under Article 53.1 of the AFC Disciplinary and Ethics Code for team misconduct after six of their players were booked during the match.
The committee noted that the incident was the club's sixth violation within the recidivism period.

The Southern Tigers were also fined US$2,250 (RM9,900) under Article 15.2 of the AFC Competition Operations Manual after their team officials caused a two-minute delay to the start of the second half. It was JDT's third countdown violation.

Munoz was separately fined US$1,500 (RM6,600) for failing to ensure his players completed their preparations and left the dressing room in accordance with the official countdown, resulting in the delay.
Buriram were handed an identical US$2,250 (RM9,100) fine for their part in the delayed restart, while head coach Mario Silva was fined US$1,500 (RM6,100).
JDT were not the only prominent Asian club to face disciplinary action, with the committee also imposing sanctions for a range of offences across the continent.

Cristiano Ronaldo's Al-Nassr and defender Mohamed Simakan received combined fines of US$22,500 (RM99,000) after the Frenchman failed to attend a mandatory flash interview following their match against UAE side Al-Ain.

The committee fined Simakan US$10,000 (RM44,000) for failing to participate in the interview despite an AFC request, while Al-Nassr were ordered to pay US$12,500 (RM55,000) for failing to ensure the player fulfilled his post-match media obligations.
The heaviest punishment went to UAE side Al-Wasl, who were fined US$80,000 (RM352,000) after their home match against Saudi Arabia's Al-Ahli descended into disorder.

According to the AFC's match reports, home supporters threw at least 80 objects, including plastic cups containing water, water bottles and a signage board, onto the pitch and surrounding areas on several occasions.

Former Melbourne Victory manager Kevin Muscat and his Chinese Super League side Shanghai Port were also fined US$1,500 each after being found to have remained in the dressing room before their match against Thailand's Ratchaburi.

All sanctioned clubs and individuals have been ordered to settle their fines within 30 days of receiving notification of the decisions, in accordance with Article 11.3 of the AFC Disciplinary and Ethics Code.
e2c85bd813053ca7: KUALA LUMPUR: The Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) has dismissed claims that the Attorney-General or other parties directed prison authorities to "act unlawfully" over Datuk Seri Najib Razak's house arrest.

0340a35f9416311b: KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Seri Najib Razak could be detained beyond the period legally permitted if the courts do not clarify whether his SRC International prison sentence has ended, the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) warned today.

"If the court decides that the sentence in the SRC International case has ended, continued detention on the basis of that sentence could result in him being detained beyond the period he should serve.
"Conversely, if the sentence remains in force, its implementation must comply with the terms of the conditional pardon and any relevant court orders," it said in a statement.
It said the legal effect of the Kuala Lumpur High Court's discharge order, issued yesterday following payment of Najib's RM50 million fine, should be referred to the court immediately.
It maintained that the move was not intended to prevent or frustrate the implementation of the royal pardon.
Instead, it said clarification was necessary to avoid conflicting interpretations of existing orders and ensure that no sentence was enforced unlawfully.
The A-GC said the discharge order raised questions over whether Najib should continue serving the remainder of his SRC sentence under house arrest or whether that sentence had legally ended.
The determination could also affect when his separate prison sentence in the 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) case begins.
The A-GC noted that the High Court had dismissed an application to stay the 1MDB sentence on Oct 14.

1cb281a3a220e7cc: PETALING JAYA: Seorang lelaki yang menaiki penerbangan dari Kuala Lumpur ditahan di Lapangan Terbang Antarabangsa Hong Kong kerana dikesan cuba menyeludup kira-kira 1kg kokain yang disorokkan dalam kasutnya.
Kastam Hong Kong memaklumkan lelaki berusia 36 tahun itu ditahan ketika pemeriksaan ke atas penumpang yang baru tiba Rabu lalu.
"Pegawai kastam menemui kira-kira 1kg bahan disyaki kokain dalam kasut dipakai lelaki berkenaan sebelum ditahan.
"Dadah yang dirampas dianggarkan bernilai HKD600,000 (kira-kira RM311,000) dan siasatan masih diteruskan," katanya dalam kenyataan di laman webnya.

Tangkapan itu menyusul beberapa kes menggunakan modus operandi sama, dengan kes terakhir seorang lelaki warga China berusia 29 tahun ditahan di Hong Kong kerana cuba menyeludup 1kg kokain disembunyikan dalam kasutnya setibanya dari Kuala Lumpur pada 16 Sept lalu.

Dua kes sama pada 7 dan 15 Julai lalu turut membabitkan kira-kira 1kg kokain dirampas daripada penumpang tiba dari Kuala Lumpur, selepas dua lagi penumpang dari Kuala Lumpur ditahan pada 17 Mei lalu dengan 820g dan 800g kokain ditemui dalam kasut mereka.
Kastam Hong Kong mengingatkan orang ramai supaya tidak menerima tawaran atau arahan pihak lain membawa barangan terkawal masuk atau keluar dari Hong Kong bagi mendapatkan ganjaran wang.
Ordinan Dadah Berbahaya Hong Kong memperuntukkan hukuman penjara maksimum seumur hidup dan denda HKD5 juta (kira-kira RM2.59 juta), jika sabit kesalahan mengedar dadah.
0850be894c07a6b0: JASIN: Ketua Barisan Nasional (BN) Johor Onn Hafiz Ghazi mempertahankan kenyataannya mengenai sindiran Pakatan Harapan (PH) hanya 'membuang masa dan wang' bertanding PRN Melaka.

95e8a4d2ef33c71f: E-bikes, noisy headphones, flytipping: Burnham is weighing in on areas that make a difference to how people feel about life Imagine waking up one morning to find a humiliating video of you, filmed without your knowledge or control, plastered all over social media. This week ministers hinted at a potential crackdown on so-called pervert glasses, wifi-enabled spectacles that let the wearer capture video of people around them, after multiple reports of men using them to harass women. ee10120876813139: Teenage ultras are increasingly causing disorder and communities fear it will not be long before it becomes something more dangerous It is five past three on Saturday afternoon and the teenage ultras of Hednesford Town are running late. As the taxi finally gets clear, the Chester gang stops in the middle of the road, shouting and gesticulating. One lad, no older than 16, pulls a long blade from inside his trousers and brandishes it. The incident ended there and no one was hurt, though a police investigation has been launched. 9e870e7690877876: DELHI: Delhi was the world's most polluted major city on Saturday morning, according to Swiss group IQAir's live ranking, as the Indian capital faced severe pollution forecasts a day before Diwali, the Hindu festival of lights.

India has ordered schools in and around Delhi to offer online classes, and encouraged people to work from home ahead of Diwali on Sunday, which is usually marked by the widespread use of firecrackers that further worsen the air quality.
IQAir ranked Delhi first among the world's major cities at 10.35 am, with a US air quality index reading of 581, double that of Lahore in neighbouring Pakistan, at 285.
IQAir's reading, based on concentrations of air pollutants, is not directly comparable to India's official index, which uses a different scale and methodology.
India's Central Pollution Control Board put Delhi's air quality index at 363 at 10am, in the "very poor" category.
Friday's air quality in Delhi was the worst pre-Diwali air in eight years, local media said, citing official data.
Pollution ​is an annual problem in many parts of northern India from the onset of winter as ⁠cold, heavy air traps vehicle emissions, construction dust and smoke from crop-waste burning.
8acfacaa7383a52b: PETALING JAYA: Golongan berpendapatan rendah (B40) dan sederhana (M40) menikmati manfaat lebih besar daripada pelaksanaan inisiatif BUDI95, berbanding golongan berpendapatan tinggi (T20), kata Menteri Kewangan II Amir Hamzah Azizan.

Beliau berkata, dapatan itu berdasarkan data penggunaan semasa yang menunjukkan corak pembelian petrol bersubsidi mengikut kumpulan pendapatan, sekali gus membolehkan kerajaan menilai agihan manfaat inisiatif berkenaan.

"Sebenarnya, sekarang saya ada data yang sempurna... kerana tiap-tiap orang yang pakai subsidi, dia guna IC (MyKad) di stesen minyak dan kita ada rekod untuk setiap pembelian yang ada dalam negara ini.
"Jadi data semasa kami menunjukkan bahawa pengedaran antara B40, M40, T20, (subsidi minyak) banyak memberi manfaat kepada M40 dengan B40," katanya menurut Bernama.

Amir Hamzah berkata, dapatan itu berbeza daripada tanggapan umum bahawa golongan T20 menggunakan lebih banyak bahan api berbanding B40 dan M40, khususnya disebabkan pemilikan kenderaan lebih besar dengan kapasiti enjin lebih tinggi.
Beliau berkata, jarak perjalanan harian juga merupakan antara faktor mempengaruhi penggunaan petrol, termasuk bagi golongan berpendapatan rendah yang tinggal jauh dari tempat kerja.

"Saya pakai andaian. Kalau saya B40, saya kerja di KL (Kuala Lumpur), saya tak duduk (tinggal) di Kenny Hills, saya tak duduk Taman Duta. Saya duduk Rawang, saya duduk Seremban. Jauh pulak. Jadi perjalanan saya akan menggunakan banyak bahan api," katanya.
Ketika ini katanya, kerajaan sedang memperhalusi angka daripada data berkenaan dan dijangka memberikan penerangan lanjut dalam tempoh dua bulan akan datang.
Amir Hamzah berkata, penjelasan itu penting bagi memperbetul persepsi masyarakat berhubung corak penggunaan serta pengagihan manfaat inisiatif BUDI95 mengikut kumpulan pendapatan.
Sebanyak 16 juta rakyat Malaysia mula menikmati manfaat inisiatif BUDI95 yang telah dilaksanakan pada 30 Sept lepas.
Inisiatif itu menetapkan harga petrol RON95 pada kadar RM1.99 seliter berbanding RM2.05 seliter sebelum ini, dengan setiap individu diberi kelayakan hingga 300 liter sebulan.
e98c94ae7dd94c20: PETALING JAYA: Anak perempuan Najib Razak, Nooryana Najwa kecewa dengan kelewatan pelaksanaan tahanan rumah bapanya, walaupun denda RM50 juta telah dilunaskan bagi memenuhi syarat pengampunan bersyarat.

"Sebagai anak, saya memang sangat kecewa. Kami telah ikut apa yang telah ditetapkan dalam perintah pengampunan bersyarat Tuanku (Sultan Ibrahim). Kami kumpul dana, kami bayar RM50 juta denda, kami ikut proses yang ditetapkan.
"Kalau ada syarat lain, kenapa tak dimaklumkan dari awal dan kalau masih ada halangan, kenapa terima bayaran RM50 juta itu (semalam)?" katanya dalam video Instagram.
Beliau berkata, episod itu mengingatkan mereka terhadap pengalaman pahit yang dilalui keluarganya berhubung titah tambahan diraja.

Beliau merujuk perintah tahanan rumah, yang dikatakan dikeluarkan pada 2024, susulan perintah pengampunan asal yang mengurangkan tempoh hukuman penjara Najib daripada 12 tahun kepada enam tahun serta jumlah denda daripada RM210 juta kepada RM50 juta.
"Terlalu banyak perkara berulang-alik, ketidaktentuan dan penangguhan demi penangguhan.

"Setiap kali kami rasa ayah dah semakin hampir nak balik, ada saja halangan baharu. Sampai bila (perkara ini perlu berlarutan)? Kami cuma mohon keadilan berterusan. Kami nak perintah Tuanku dihormati dan kedaulatan undang-undang ditegakkan."
Beliau merujuk cadangan Jabatan Peguam Negara (AGC) semalam supaya pelaksanaan tahanan rumah Najib ditangguhkan sehingga penelitian terhadap pengampunan bersyarat dan Perintah Pelepasan selesai.
AGC berkata, dua isu itu membabitkan "persoalan undang-undang rumit" dan mempunyai implikasi terhadap pelaksanaan perintah pengampunan diraja serta satu perintah mahkamah.

Bagaimanapun, Istana Negara dalam kenyataan hari ini memaklumkan Yang di-Pertuan Agong, Sultan Ibrahim menegaskan perintah pengampunan bersyarat itu jelas, nyata dan tanpa sebarang ambiguti, selain tiada kaitan dengan mana-mana kes lain membabitkan bekas perdana menteri itu.
Istana Negara turut menegaskan tidak sepatutnya timbul kekeliruan tafsiran atau ketidakpastian berpanjangan mengenai pelaksanaan keputusan yang diperkenankan.

"Memandangkan semua syarat di dalam perintah pengampunan bersyarat itu telah dipenuhi, sebarang hujah mempertikaikan perintah tersebut adalah menjurus ke arah mengingkari perintah Yang di-Pertuan Agong," menurut kenyataan Istana Negara.
99d7531c803f36cc: NEW DELHI: India fast bowler Mohammed Shami said he would continue playing white-ball cricket and remain available for domestic multi-day matches after retiring from test cricket on Friday, bringing the curtain down on a 13-year red-ball career.

The 36-year-old, who took 229 wickets in 64 tests after making a memorable debut against West Indies in 2013, announced his decision in a video posted on social media on the anniversary of his first test appearance.
"Let's end this 13-year journey here today," Shami said.
"I made my debut today, and today I am taking retirement. I am leaving this, but I will continue to play white-ball cricket, whether it is IPL or domestic.
"If it is needed for fitness, I will continue to play days cricket. So, this was the journey so far. I started it today, and I am ending it today."

His final test appearance came in the World Test Championship final against Australia in 2023, but he continued to play limited-overs cricket before injuries and fitness concerns hampered his appearances for India.

Shami, India's all-time leading wicket-taker in 50-over World Cups with 55 wickets, last featured for India in a one-day international against New Zealand last year and in a Twenty20 match against England in February 2025.
He currently represents Bengal in domestic cricket and plays for Lucknow Super Giants in the Indian Premier League. - Reuters
c6c098db8724cdec: PETALING JAYA: The Budi RON95 initiative has benefited the B40 and M40 income groups the most, says finance minister II Amir Hamzah Azizan.
He said these groups have derived greater benefits from the implementation of the fuel subsidy compared with those from the T20 group, Bernama reported.
Amir added that this conclusion is based on current consumption data, which allows the government to identify patterns in the purchase of subsidised petrol across different income groups.
"In fact, I now have perfect data because everyone who utilises the subsidy uses their MyKad at the petrol station, and we have a record of every single purchase made in the country.
"So, our current data shows that the distribution of fuel subsidies provides the most benefit to the M40 and B40 groups," he said during a podcast featured on the "Duit Faiz" TikTok account.
Amir added that the government is currently refining the figures based on this data and is expected to provide further details within the next two months.

He pointed out that the findings contradict the common perception that the T20 group consumes more fuel than the B40 and M40 groups, a belief often attributed to the assumption that the T20 group owns more vehicles with larger engine capacities.
Amir said it was important to correct public perception regarding the distribution of benefits under the BUDI95 initiative across different income groups.

Under the BUDI95 initiative, the price of RON95 petrol is set at RM1.99 per litre, down from the previous price of RM2.05 per litre, with each individual entitled to a quota of up to 300 litres per month.
Only Malaysians can enjoy the fuel subsidy, as the MyKad is required when filling up at the petrol station.
8ff72f323321a758: JASIN: Sayap Pemuda Umno dan PAS akan menggerakkan laporan polis di seluruh negara terhadap Peguam Negara Dusuki Mokhtar berhubung keputusan tidak melaksanakan titah tahanan rumah melibatkan bekas perdana menteri, Najib Razak.

f530855e6ac5ca21: PETALING JAYA: Najib Razak’s daughter, Nooryana Najwa, has expressed disappointment over the delay in implementing her father's house arrest following the payment of the RM50 million fine in fulfillment of the conditional pardon order.

c163383e47c1b35a: RHO (Italy), Nov 7 — Just as with electric cars, Chinese motorcycle brands are roaring into European markets, with high-performance, cut-price models starting to make a name for themselves.
At EICMA in Milan, Europe’s biggest motorcycle show, visitors were jostling on Friday around the stand of CFMoto, one of the main Chinese brands sold in Europe.
The firm from Hangzhou has gained attention by producing engines and assembling models for Austria’s KTM, then by winning two Moto3 (250cc) championships in 2024 and 2026.
Fans of BMW, Honda and Ducati came to Milan to admire a powerful model fitted with winglets, as well as the off-road machine ridden by the brand’s new ambassador, Spanish rider Mario Roman.

“They’re beautiful. They may not have exactly the same materials... as the Japanese manufacturers, but at this price, it works,” said Renato Polistene, a 64-year-old Italian craftsman, who was looking at the stand.

Currently riding a KTM, Polistene said he could consider choosing Chinese for his next bike, especially because prices for other brands “have gone up a lot” and they tack on “too many options” to the base price.

In 2025 China became the EU’s second-largest supplier of motorcycles, behind Japan, accounting for 27.1 per cent of imports with sales at one billion euros (RM4.68 billion), according to a report published Thursday by the European Association of Motorcycle Manufacturers (ACEM).
The growth has been spectacular in the most powerful models, a segment traditionally dominated by European and Japanese manufacturers.

In six years, China has gone from a marginal supplier to a key player in the European market: it now accounts for nearly one-third of imports of motorcycles over 250cc, compared with just seven per cent in 2019.
The European press, which first looked at the bikes with scepticism, now tests them like any others in its comparison reviews.
For British magazine Motorcycle News, 2026 is “the year where we see a switch.”

At the Cyclone brand’s stand, a band was belting out “Volare” at full blast while hostesses threw T-shirts bearing the name of the brand of the Zonsen group from Chongqing, China’s two-wheeler industry capital.
Another Chinese giant, Qianjiang Motorcycle (QJ Motor), has itself become a little Italian by buying in 2005 one of the country’s national prides, Benelli.

New startups are joining the big established names, like ZXMoto, founded by Zhang Xue, a former mechanic and rider.

Alessia, 27, a police officer from Turin who did not wish to give her last name, had come to look at her next Triumph model but stopped at the ZXMoto stand.
“I was really impressed by the design,” she told AFP, noting that new brands on the market can “spark curiosity”.
‘Revolution’
In the French market, it’s “a true revolution coming from the East,” wrote Bertrand Mace, president of the two wheel division of French automotive association Mobilians, in a press release.
CFMoto established itself in October as the fifth brand on the French market, overtaking long-standing players such as Triumph, Suzuki, KTM, and Yamaha.
In its wake, Zontes has doubled its sales in a year, and QJMotor and Voge are booming, according to Mobilians.
“Aggressive pricing, combined with an undeniable move upmarket, is hitting the mark with customers whose purchasing power is under pressure,” said Mace.
At the CFMoto stand, executives from a major Italian brand stopped by on Wednesday to have a look at the high-speed sport bike.

120b05daad59af04: SEOUL, Nov 7 — South Korean cryptocurrency exchange GOPAX said Friday it had suspended withdrawals and trading as an emergency measure following hacking threats, Yonhap News Agency reported.
The exchange said it halted withdrawals at 2.55pm and was transferring most of the assets held in its so-called hot wallets to cold wallets, which are not connected to the internet.
It also suspended trading at around 3.53pm.
GOPAX said it had yet to verify the credibility of the hacking threat but had taken precautionary action to protect customers’ assets.
No actual loss of assets had been reported, it added.

All outstanding orders were cancelled following the suspension of trading.
“We received an email from a group claiming to have hacked the exchange, but we have yet to verify whether the threat is genuine,” a company official, who asked not to be named, said.
“We are prioritising the protection of customers’ assets, even if this causes inconvenience to users.”
The South Korean financial sector has recently been hit by a series of cybersecurity incidents.

ca8187dc18d8d6b4: From P Kamalanathan

Deepavali is here again. In every Hindu home, the oil lamps are lit, the kolam is drawn, the house is filled with the smell of murukku, nei urundai and payasam, and children run around in new clothes, waiting for the first burst of fireworks.
But beyond the celebration, Deepavali carries a timeless message that we must never forget: Light must triumph over darkness.
Thiruvalluvar said it beautifully more than 2,000 years ago:
Those who seek the Divine will be freed from the darkness of life.
That darkness is not just outside us. It is also within us; anger, jealousy, hatred, selfishness, and division.
Deepavali reminds us to light a lamp inside ourselves first.
Deepavali is also a celebration of our identity

For Malaysians of Indian origin, Deepavali is not just a festival. It is a reminder of who we are, where we come from, and what we carry forward for our children. Our language, our culture, our values, our faith, these are the lamps we must keep burning.

Just this week, we saw how important it is to protect that light. When there was a proposal to reduce Tamil language hours in our Tamil schools from 12 to 10 periods, our community spoke up together; teachers, parents, PTAs, leaders, and ordinary families. And I am grateful that the education ministry listened and decided not to pursue it.
That is the spirit of Deepavali. When we stand together in light, darkness cannot win.
Deepavali is a Malaysian celebration

In Malaysia, Deepavali is not celebrated only by Indians. Our Malay, Chinese, Kadazan, Iban and Orang Asli friends join us at our open houses, taste our food, wear Indian clothes, and share our joy. That is the true beauty of Malaysia, unity in diversity, not just in words, but in our homes.

As a former deputy education minister, I have always believed that our greatest strength is our children. If we teach them to respect all races and religions, to love their own mother tongue while embracing Bahasa Malaysia and English, to be kind and to be disciplined; then Malaysia’s future will be bright.
This Deepavali, let us make three promises:
1. Light a lamp for unity Let us reject hatred and division, and choose understanding.
2. Light a lamp for education Let us encourage our children to study hard, to read our mother tongue language, to master knowledge, and to be proud of their heritage.
3. Light a lamp for kindness Let us remember the poor, the lonely, and those who are struggling. Share a meal. Visit an old folks’ home. Help a neighbour. That is the true Deepavali.
To all Malaysians, I wish you a Happy Deepavali.
May your home be filled with light, your family with love, and your life with health and prosperity.
P Kamalanathan is a former deputy education minister and an FMT reader.

2172131c972baeee: Saya angkat songkok kepada Umno sambil ucap tahniah dan syabas kerana berjaya kutip RM50 juta dengan cepat dan pantas bagi membolehkan bekas presiden Najib Razak menjalani baki hukuman penjara di rumah.
Kita tentu masih ingat Umno mula pungut wang September lalu. Semalam RM50 juta sudah dapat dikumpulkan. Kurang tiga bulan. Satu pencapaian menakjubkan.

Itu sebab saya kata Umno 'terer'. Power. Orang lain terkial-kial cari dana untuk capai sasaran jauh yang lebih kurang daripada jumlah yang Umno kumpulkan dengan mudah. Misalnya, ada banyak NGO bertungkus-lumus cari sumbangan orang ramai dan syarikat untuk umpamanya membiayai pembedahan jantung kanak-kanak. Media juga diminta membantu untuk menghebahkan usaha mereka supaya matlamat tercapai. Usaha itu mungkin membuahkan hasil tetapi ada kala mengambil masa berbulan-bulan atau lebih lama.

Tetapi Umno dapat pungut RM50 juta bagai sekelip mata, menyebabkan saya angkat songkok dengan penuh rasa kagum. Saya cadang NGO minta pertolongan Umno lain kali mahu cari dana untuk biaya rawatan pesakit yang tidak berkemampuan, atau belajar daripada Umno rahsia memungut wang dengan pantas.

To put things in context, kita imbau kembali. Najib dipenjarakan pada Ogos 2022 selepas Mahkamah Persekutuan mengekalkan sabitan atas kesalahan menyalahguna kuasa, pecah amanah dan pengubahan wang haram membabitkan dana RM42 juta milik SRC International. Beliau dihukum penjara 12 tahun dan denda RM210 juta.

Pun begitu pada Januari 2024, Yang di-Pertuan Agong ketika itu Al-Sultan Abdullah Sultan Ahmad Shah mengurangkan separuh hukuman itu dan menurunkan jumlah denda kepada RM50 juta menerusi pengampunan diraja. Pada September lalu, Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim memberikan Najib pengampunan bersyarat yang membolehkan dia menjalani baki hukuman di bawah tahanan rumah sehingga 23 Ogos 2028.

Tetapi tahanan di rumah hanya boleh dilaksanakan jika Najib bayar denda RM50 juta serta pematuhan syarat-syarat lain yang ditetapkan. Syarat-syarat itu membabitkan urusan pemenjaraan. Yang paling utama ialah Najib mesti bayar RM50 juta, barulah boleh nikmati tahanan di rumah, di kediaman yang terletak di kawasan elit di ibu negara.

Berikutan itu, Umno lancar Tabung Solidariti Najib Razak pada 18 Sept lalu, tujuannya untuk kumpul RM50 juta. Menurut Setiausaha Agung Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki, setakat Ogos lalu, Wanita Umno ada 1,412,052 ahli. Pemuda Umno ada 418,062 ahli. Puteri Umno pula 226,076 ahli. Jadi jumlah keseluruhan ahli Umno ialah 3,251,456 orang.

Saya tidak tahu sama ada si setiausaha agung Umno ada ambil kira jumlah ahli yang tinggalkan parti. Lazimnya orang yang keluar parti akan angkat kaki begitu sahaja. Mereka tidak akan maklumkan kepada ibu pejabat Umno. Saya merujuk kepada ahli biasa yang tak terkenal.

Tidak usah pertikai jumlah ahli Umno yang diumumkan si setiausaha agung parti. Take it as it is, ertinya ada tiga juta lebih ahli. Senang cerita genapkan kepada empat juta ahli Umno maka jika setiap ahli sumbang RM1 untuk tabung Najib, dapat kumpul RM4 juta sahaja. Bagaimanapun takkanlah mereka sumbang RM1 sahaja -- mungkin ada yang sumbang RM50, RM100 atau RM1,000. Tentu ada yang beri lebih daripada itu.

Teringat saya laporan media 21 Sept lalu yang memetik isteri Najib, Rosmah Mansor, menzahirkan rasa terharu kerana rakan-rakan dari Singapura, Brunei, Itali dan Kanada menghulur sumbangan untuk bantu Najib. Mungkin jumlah yang dinyatakan Rosmah itu disalurkan kepada tabung anjuran Umno.

Sememangnya RM50 juta itu satu jumlah besar. Semalam Asyraf dengan bangga dan gembira mengumumkan partinya sudah berjaya kumpul dana mencukupi menerusi kempen sumbangan untuk Najib, dan Umno sudah menjelaskan denda RM50 juta untuk Najib.
"Kami ingin mengucapkan terima kasih kepada ahli-ahli dan orang ramai atas sumbangan mereka," kata Asyraf menerusi kenyataan.

Muncul bekas Ahli Parlimen Damansara Tony Pua menggesa pihak berkuasa mengaudit sumbangan yang dikutip. Kata beliau, audit oleh Bank Negara dan Suruhanjaya Pencegahan Rasuah Malaysia penting bagi memastikan dana yang dikumpulkan diperoleh secara sah dan bukan hasil pengubahan wang haram. Saya setuju.
Dalam pada itu, Pua berpendapat adalah lebih elok jika wang yang Umno kumpul digunakan untuk bantu rakyat biasa. Memang betul tetapi jelas Umno has its own priorities.
Artikel ini adalah pandangan penulis dan tidak semestinya mewakili FMT.

72a4d55ba96bb0e6: WASHINGTON: Production of Cybertrucks -- the pickups hailed by enthusiasts as a symbol of Elon Musk's futuristic ambitions and equally hated as ugly reminders of the Donald Trump era -- will wind down, the Tesla CEO said Friday.
Tesla will stop building the truck at its Texas factory around the middle of 2027 to free up space for its Cybercab robotaxi, Musk said.
"Tesla will be winding down production of the Cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production," Musk wrote on X.
Musk did not say whether the truck would be built elsewhere or discontinued altogether, nor what would happen to outstanding orders.
Wes Morrill, the Cybertruck's lead engineer, wrote in a separate post that the truck "was an incredible technology development platform and lives on through Cybercab."
